ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r1.claim: Poetry uses al-aʿrāf for a high place, as in comparisons to a mountain crest and upright lances; horse and rooster crests take the same name because they rise above the body.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r1.anchor: ومنه عرف الفرس وعرف الديك لعلوهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r2.claim: The word six comes from an older form sidsa, with consonant substitutions and assimilation; its diminutive preserves the older sīn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r2.anchor: الستة رتبة من العدد معروفة وأصلها سدسة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r3.speaker: الليث
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r3.claim: Al-Layth glosses exhorting as hastening someone; its agent is described as eager or urged on.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r3.anchor: الحث الإعجال حثثت فلانا فأحثثت قاله الليث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the command for justice as the declaration that there is no god but God, since all good begins from it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس القسط هنا لا إله إلا الله لأن أسباب الخير كلها تنشأ عنها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r5.speaker: عطاء والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r5.claim: Ata and al-Suddi take justice as fairness, or as speech that is visibly good and correct.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r5.anchor: وقال عطاء والسدي: العدل وما يظهر في القول كونه حسنا صوابا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r6.claim: Other glosses of justice are truth and what is right.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r7.claim: Grammatically, establish your faces can coordinate with the verbal noun justice by supplying that you establish; command verbs can be governed by the particle that, unlike a merely nominal maṣdar particle or a source-like kay.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r7.anchor: وأقيموا معطوف على ما ينحل إليه المصدر الذي هو القسط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari instead supplies and say before the imperative, either making it dependent on that verb or joining it to the first command say.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r8.anchor: جعل الزمخشري وأقيموا على تقدير وقل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r9.claim: Another grammatical proposal joins the command to an omitted imperative such as turn toward God, then establish your faces.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r9.anchor: وقيل: وأقيموا معطوف على أمر محذوف تقديره فأقبلوا وأقيموا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r10.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك وابن قتيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r10.claim: They say that when prayer comes, people should pray in every mosque rather than insist on their own mosque.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والضحاك واختاره ابن قتيبة: المعنى إذا حضرت الصلاة فصلوا في كل مسجد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r11.speaker: مجاهد والسدي وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r11.claim: They interpret the command as facing the Kaʿba in prayer wherever one is.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد والسدي وابن زيد: معناه توجهوا حيث كنتم في الصلاة إلى الكعبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r12.speaker: الربيع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r12.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says to make prostration sincere to God alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r12.anchor: وقال الربيع: اجعلوا سجودكم خالصا لله دون غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r13.speaker: الماوردي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r13.claim: Al-Mawardi says to go to a mosque at each prayer time, making the verse an instruction to pray in congregation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r14.speaker: التبريزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r14.claim: Al-Tabrizi says that if a mosque is nearby, people should establish congregational prayer there rather than go elsewhere.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r15.speaker: الربيع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r15.claim: A further explanation from al-Rabiʿ is to bring intention to God in every prayer and direct oneself toward Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r15.anchor: وقيل هو أمر بإحضار النية لله في كل صلاة والقصد نحوه كما تقول وجهت وجهي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r16.claim: Another interpretation permits prayer anywhere on earth, since every place is a mosque where one must worship God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p37/r16.anchor: وقيل معناه إباحة الصلاة في كل موضع من الأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains establish your faces as directing worship uprightly toward God at every prayer time and every place of prostration.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r1.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أي اقصدوا عبادته مستقيمين إليه غير عادلين إلى غيرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r2.claim: The command to call on God may mean literal supplication, worship, or saying there is no god but God; supplication requires exclusive devotion to be answered.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r2.anchor: قيل: الدعاء على بابه أمر به مقرونا بالإخلاص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r3.claim: They explain returning as resurrection: just as God originated people, He recreates them after death to reward their deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن وقتادة هو إعلام بالبعث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari gives only the resurrection interpretation, arguing that initial creation answers denial of return and calls for sincere worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r4.anchor: قال: كما أنشأكم ابتداء يعيدكم احتج عليهم في إنكارهم الإعادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r5.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj likewise argues that raising people is no harder than first creating them and answers their denial of resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r5.anchor: وهذا احتجاج عليهم في إنكارهم البعث انتهى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر بن عبد الله وأبو العالية ومحمد بن كعب وابن جبير والسدي ومجاهد والفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r6.claim: A second interpretation says people return in the camps of belief and happiness or unbelief and misery already decreed for them; a similar meaning is reported from the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وجابر بن عبد الله وأبو العالية ومحمد بن كعب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r7.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r7.claim: Ubayy’s reading says you return as two groups, one guided and one condemned to error, supporting the two-camps interpretation and making the second group a circumstantial phrase.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r7.anchor: قراءة أبي تعودون فريقين فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqa parses one group as the object of guided and the other as the object of an implied misled, or takes both clauses as circumstances with an omitted qad.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r8.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون فريقا مفعول هدى وفريقا مفعول أضل مضمرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r9.claim: Other readings say people return unsupported, return from dust to dust, or rise naked as they were created; the first echoes the Quran’s description of arriving alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r9.anchor: وقيل المعنى تعودون لا ناصر لكم ولا معين لقوله ولقد جئتمونا فرادى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r10.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r10.claim: Hasan says people are returned to dust just as they began from dust.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن: كما بدأكم من التراب يعيدكم إلى التراب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r11.claim: Another interpretation says people are created unclothed and resurrected unclothed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r11.anchor: وقيل: معناه كما خلقكم عراة تبعثون عراة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r12.claim: The phrase about error being established may mean God decreed error for them or that the punishment for error became due.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r12.anchor: ومعنى حق عليهم الضلالة أي حق عليهم من الله أو حق عليهم عقوبة الضلالة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r13.claim: Though God is the guide and creates misguidance, the wording does not attribute misguidance to Him because the passage addresses Satan’s misleading and God’s command to justice and prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p38/r13.anchor: وجاء إسناد الهدى إلى الله ولم يجىء مقابله وفريقا أضل

TABATABAI:7:26-36#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#4/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:26-36#4/r1.claim: One report interprets establishing one’s face at every mosque as facing the qibla; the author calls it an application of the verse.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسكان عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سألته عن قول الله عز وجل { وأقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد }

TABATABAI:7:26-36#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#4/r2.speaker: زرارة وحمران ومحمد بن مسلم
TABATABAI:7:26-36#4/r2.claim: Reports from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq explain the instruction as facing the Kaaba from mosques established across the lands; the author links this to the later qibla ruling in 2:144.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#4/r2.anchor: عن زرارة وحمران ومحمد بن مسلم عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليهما السلام

TABATABAI:7:26-36#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:26-36#4/r3.claim: Because al-A‘raf is Meccan and the Kaaba became the qibla in Medina, this verse may state the general command, with the Medinan verse later specifying its direction.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#4/r3.anchor: والآية التي نحن فيها وهي من سورة الاعراف مكية

TABATABAI:7:26-36#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#4/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:26-36#4/r4.claim: A report from al-Sadiq interprets ‘establish your faces’ as the Imams; the author takes this to mean congregational prayer leaders, with another possible sense to follow.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#4/r4.anchor: عن الحسين بن مهران عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله { وأقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد } يعني الأئمة

TABATABAI:7:26-36#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#8/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:26-36#8/r5.claim: A report says people were created as believers or unbelievers, happy or wretched, and return on Judgment Day as guided or astray; Ali ibn Ibrahim also quotes the Prophet that happiness or misery is fixed in the womb.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#8/r5.anchor: في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله { كما بدأكم تعودون

TABATABAI:7:26-36#8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#8/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:26-36#8/r6.claim: Though Abu al-Jarud is criticized, transmitters accepted his reports from al-Baqir before his deviation; other reports also convey the return’s resemblance to the beginning.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#8/r6.anchor: القوم قبلوا ما رواه عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في حال استقامته

TABATABAI:7:26-36#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:26-36#9/r1.claim: He rejects essential, inescapable happiness or misery: it would make education, moral judgment, law, revelation, and completing the proof against people meaningless, and would limit God’s sovereignty.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#9/r1.anchor: ولا معنى لإتمام الحجة في الذاتيات بأي معنى صورناها

TABATABAI:7:26-36#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:26-36#9/r2.claim: The Quran affirms human choice: God creates people, grants reason to distinguish good from evil, then tests them through religious duties; obedience yields reward and disobedience punishment.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#9/r2.anchor: والدار دار امتحان وابتلاء، والعمل اليوم والجزاء غدا

TABATABAI:7:26-36#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:26-36#9/r3.claim: This account rests on two premises: voluntary action differs from involuntary action, and chosen acts can be morally good or bad and merit praise, blame, reward, or punishment.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#9/r3.anchor: إحداهما أن بين الفعل الاختياري وغيره فرقا

TABATABAI:7:26-36#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:26-36#10/r1.claim: General reports that humanity was created as two groups match verses describing believers and unbelievers; the division is initially general and each person’s outcome becomes definite through chosen deeds and guidance or satanic influence.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#10/r1.anchor: الذي في بدء الخلقة قضاء مشروط ثم يخرج عن الاشتراط إلى الإطلاق بالأعمال الاختيارية

TABATABAI:7:26-36#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#10/r2.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:26-36#10/r2.claim: Al-Sajjad says God made the Shia from a high heavenly clay, their enemies from Sijjin, and the enemies’ allies from an even lower clay.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#10/r2.anchor: عن علي بن الحسين عليه السلام أنه قال أخذ الله ميثاق شيعتنا معنا على ولايتنا

TABATABAI:7:26-36#10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#10/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:26-36#10/r3.claim: Asked why some non-Shia show fine manners while some Shia behave badly, al-Sadiq says human clay was mixed from Paradise and Fire and people return toward the material that marked them.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#10/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن كيسان قال قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام جعلت فداك أنا مولاك

TABATABAI:7:26-36#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#10/r4.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:26-36#10/r4.claim: Ali is reported to say Adam was created from varied earth—salty, barren, and wholesome—and his descendants include the righteous and wicked.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#10/r4.anchor: عن حبة العرني عن علي عليه السلام قال إن الله خلق آدم من أديم الأرض

TABATABAI:7:26-36#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:26-36#11/r1.claim: He connects the clay reports to the Quranic books of the wicked in Sijjin and the righteous in Illiyun.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#11/r1.anchor: إن كتاب الفجار لفي سجين وما أدراك ما سجين

TABATABAI:7:26-36#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#11/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:26-36#11/r2.claim: The report about Adam’s diverse earth suggests material constitution influences human traits, as different materials shape the forms and effects that arise from them, but only as a predisposition, not a complete cause.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#11/r2.anchor: وإن كان ذلك على الاقتضاء دون العلية التامة

TABATABAI:7:26-36#11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:26-36#11/r3.claim: He interprets Paradise or Fire clay as earthly matter that ultimately becomes part of the corresponding afterlife realm through a person’s development and deeds.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#11/r3.anchor: إنما يسلك إلى كل منهما ما يناسبها في مادة الخلقة

TABATABAI:7:26-36#12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#12/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:26-36#12/r1.claim: Healthy temperaments can produce finer spirits, understanding, and emotions that incline people toward sound belief, intention, and action; the same process applies to misery.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#12/r1.anchor: تنشأ ذوات أرواح لطيفة لها عقول جيدة وعواطف رقيقة تميل بالإنسان إلى ما فيه صلاح إنسانيته من العقائد والإرادات والأعمال

TABATABAI:7:26-36#12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#12/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:26-36#12/r2.claim: Good temperaments and spirits incline people toward sound belief, intention, and action; the influences accumulate toward an outcome, with the same reasoning applying to misery.
TABATABAI:7:26-36#12/r2.anchor: لها عقول جيدة وعواطف رقيقة تميل بالإنسان إلى ما فيه صلاح إنسانيته

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p27/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p27/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p27/.claim: Qisṭ, or fairness, is the comprehensive balance underlying the sharī‘ah and all religious directives.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p27/.anchor: Qisṭ is an all-embracing reality which is also the essence of the sharī‘ah.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p27/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p27/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p27/.claim: Fairness applies across beliefs, deeds, morals, worship, economics, politics, and society.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p27/.anchor: It is inclusive of beliefs, deeds, morality, worship as well as directives related to economics, politics and society.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p27/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p27/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p27/.claim: Since God is master, fairness requires worship of Him alone; since He created and sustains people, fairness also requires accountability and recompense.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p27/.anchor: when God is the master, then it is against fairness to worship someone other than Him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p27/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p27/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p27/.claim: If God did not hold people accountable and reward or punish them, that would be injustice rather than fairness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p27/.anchor: then He should hold them accountable and reward or punish them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p28/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p28/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p28/.claim: A mosque and prostration belong to God alone, so worshippers should not face or invoke anyone else; Islahi cites 72:18.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p28/.anchor: Prostration is due before God only and hence a mosque by its very nature is specific for God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p28/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p28/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p28/.claim: The parallel wording about sincerity shows that obedience, like worship, is owed exclusively to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p28/.anchor: They show that it is not just God’s worship that entails sincerity, His obedience also entails sincerity; none else can be included in it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p28/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p28/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p28/.claim: People should worship and obey their Creator alone because they return to Him alone, without alleged deities or intercessors.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p28/.anchor: just as they came into this world alone, they will go back to Him alone; none of their alleged deities and intercessors will be with them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p28/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p28/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p28/.claim: The concise return-to-God statement links the afterlife with monotheism and points to an evident proof of the afterlife.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p28/.anchor: a very evident proof of the hereafter is also pointed to.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p29/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p29/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p29/.claim: Addressing people as Adam’s children reminds Quraysh and the Arabs that Satan is humanity’s eternal enemy and following him means befriending their father’s foe.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p29/.anchor: It gives this message to every human being that Satan is their eternal enemy.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p34#3/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p34#3/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p34#3/r1.claim: بدأ الشيء means to originate and invent it.

FARRA:v1p375/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p375/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p375/r4.claim: Just as God began creation with people either wretched or blessed, they will return in corresponding states of wretchedness or blessedness.
FARRA:v1p375/r4.anchor: يقول: بدأكم في الخلق شقيا وسعيدا

FARRA:v1p375/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p375/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p375/r7.claim: أقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد means to pray at any mosque where prayer time catches one; outside prayer time, one may pray wherever one wishes.
FARRA:v1p375/r7.anchor: إذا أدركتك الصلاة وأنت عند مسجد فصل فيه

STUDYQURAN:7:29/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r1.claim: Qisṭ means justice, and here answers the disbelievers' allegation that God commands indecency; it can also mean what is right or proper.
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r1.anchor: not indecency, as the disbelievers allege in v. 28.

STUDYQURAN:7:29/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r2.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r2.claim: Some connect qisṭ with the testimony of faith, following the verse where God and knowledgeable witnesses uphold justice.
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r2.anchor: connected by some with the testimony of faith, “There is no god but God,” following 3:18

STUDYQURAN:7:29/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r3.claim: Setting one's face means facing the qiblah toward the Sacred Mosque in Makkah.
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r3.anchor: toward the qiblah, or direction of prayer, which is toward the Sacred Mosque in Makkah

STUDYQURAN:7:29/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r4.claim: One possible reading is to face the qiblah at every place one prays, wherever one may be.
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r4.anchor: turn toward the qiblah in prayer “wheresoever you may be”

STUDYQURAN:7:29/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r5.claim: Another possible reading is to face the qiblah at every prayer time.
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r5.anchor: the verse could also mean to turn toward the qiblah at every time of prayer

STUDYQURAN:7:29/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r6.claim: Turning or submitting one's face to God is a Quranic image for orienting one's whole being toward worship and obedience.
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r6.anchor: signifying the orientation of one’s whole being toward worship of and obedience to God

STUDYQURAN:7:29/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r7.claim: Calling upon God most commonly means supplicating Him for spiritual and material needs.
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r7.anchor: To call upon Him most commonly means to supplicate God for one’s spiritual and material needs

STUDYQURAN:7:29/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r8.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r8.claim: Some commentators instead take calling upon God here to mean canonical prayer or worship generally.
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r8.anchor: some commentators here consider it a reference to canonical prayer or worship generally

STUDYQURAN:7:29/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r9.claim: Devoting religion entirely to God connotes sincere worship for His sake alone, a phrase often following the command to call upon Him.
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r9.anchor: a phrase connoting sincere worship for the sake of God alone

STUDYQURAN:7:29/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r10.claim: The analogy between original creation and resurrection shows that God's recognized creative power should dispel doubts about His ability to resurrect people.
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r10.anchor: indicates the analogous nature of original creation and resurrection

STUDYQURAN:7:29/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r11.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r11.claim: A hadith says people will be resurrected as they were born: barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised, alone and dependent on God.
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r11.anchor: According to a ḥadīth, people will be resurrected in the same state as that in which they were born

STUDYQURAN:7:29/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r12.claim: The creation-resurrection parallel is echoed in 6:94 and elsewhere.
STUDYQURAN:7:29/r12.anchor: See 6:94: And [God will say], “Now you have come unto Us alone, just as We created you the first time”

TABATABAI:7:29/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:29/r1.claim: After the preceding verse denies that God commands indecency, this verse states God's actual command, the opposite of what was falsely ascribed to Him.
TABATABAI:7:29/r1.anchor: لما نفت الآية السابقة أن يأمر الله سبحانه بالفحشاء وذكرت أن ذلك افتراء عليه

TABATABAI:7:29/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29/r2.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:7:29/r2.claim: Al-Raghib defines qist as a just share; taking another's share is injustice, while giving it fairly is equity, so qasata means injustice and aqsata means justice.
TABATABAI:7:29/r2.anchor: والقسط على ما ذكره الراغب هو النصيب بالعدل كالنصف والنصفة

TABATABAI:7:29/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:29/r3.claim: God's command to qist means keeping to the just middle in all affairs, avoiding excess and deficiency; in worship it means devoting oneself to God alone without idolatry or imitation of ancestors and leaders.
TABATABAI:7:29/r3.anchor: فالمراد قل أمر ربي بالنصيب العدل ولزوم وسط الاعتدال في الأمور كلها وأن تجتنبوا جانبي الإفراط والتفريط

TABATABAI:7:29/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:29/r4.claim: The command to establish one's faces is coordinated with the quoted command: since 'my Lord commands justice' implies 'be just,' the construction means 'be just and establish your faces.'
TABATABAI:7:29/r4.anchor: فقوله { وأقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد } معطوف ظاهرا على مقول القول لأن معنى أمر ربي بالقسط أقسطوا

TABATABAI:7:29/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:29/r5.claim: The face is what turns toward an object; establishing it means fully carrying out the act, so the command calls for wholehearted devotion in worship and exclusive orientation to God, remembering Him alone during ritual.
TABATABAI:7:29/r5.anchor: والوجه هو ما يتوجه به إلى الشيء

TABATABAI:7:29/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29/r6.speaker: المفسرون
TABATABAI:7:29/r6.claim: Some exegetes take the phrase to mean facing the qibla while praying in each mosque; al-Tabataba'i rejects this historical fit because the sura is Meccan and the Kaaba was not yet the qibla.
TABATABAI:7:29/r6.anchor: وللمفسرين في معنى قوله { وأقيموا وجوهكم } الخ

TABATABAI:7:29/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29/r7.speaker: المفسرون
TABATABAI:7:29/r7.claim: Another exegetical reading is to face the divinely commanded direction, the Kaaba, at prayer times; al-Tabataba'i's historical objection is that the verse is Meccan and the Kaaba was not yet the qibla.
TABATABAI:7:29/r7.anchor: ومنها أن المعنى توجهوا في أوقات السجود وهي أوقات الصلاة إلى الجهة التي أمركم الله بها وهي الكعبة

TABATABAI:7:29/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29/r8.speaker: المفسرون
TABATABAI:7:29/r8.claim: A third reported reading says that whoever finds prayer underway at a mosque should pray there rather than wait to return to his own mosque; the author groups it among readings that do not fit the Meccan setting and lack multiple Muslim mosques.
TABATABAI:7:29/r8.anchor: ومنها إذا أدركتم الصلاة في مسجد فصلوا ولا تقولوا حتى أرجع إلى مسجدي

TABATABAI:7:29/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29/r9.speaker: المفسرون
TABATABAI:7:29/r9.claim: A further reported interpretation is to make for the mosque at every prayer for which congregational prayer has been prescribed.
TABATABAI:7:29/r9.anchor: ومنها أن المعنى اقصدوا المسجد في وقت كل صلاة أمر فيها بالجماعة

TABATABAI:7:29/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29/r10.speaker: المفسرون
TABATABAI:7:29/r10.claim: The final reported reading is to direct one's face to God in obedience without associating anything with Him; al-Tabataba'i finds it close to his interpretation but incomplete because it repeats the following clause about sincere religion.
TABATABAI:7:29/r10.anchor: وآخر الوجوه وإن كان قريبا مما قدمناه إلا أنه ناقص في بيان الإخلاص المستفاد من الآية

TABATABAI:7:29-30/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29-30/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:29-30/r1.claim: The phrase 'a party guided and a party deserving error' is a circumstantial clause for 'you return'; the shared comparison is that people return in two parties as they began in two parties.
TABATABAI:7:29-30/r1.anchor: ظاهر السياق أن يكون قوله { فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة } حالا من فاعل { تعودون } ويكون هو الوجه المشترك

TABATABAI:7:29-30/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29-30/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:29-30/r2.claim: Al-Tabataba'i compares the wording with 6:94, where people come alone as God first created them; here the explicit shared feature is instead division into two groups.
TABATABAI:7:29-30/r2.anchor: نظير قوله تعالى ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة الأنعام 94

TABATABAI:7:29-30/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29-30/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:29-30/r3.claim: He rejects proposed comparisons that leave the point of likeness unstated, such as being solitary at both beginnings, both creations from dust, or the resurrection and first creation sharing God's power; these readings omit the comparison and add needless ambiguity.

TABATABAI:7:29-30/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29-30/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:29-30/r4.claim: The apparent 'beginning' is the first worldly creation of humankind, not the whole worldly life contrasted with the afterlife: the audience is humanity, so its beginning is the species' first appearance.
TABATABAI:7:29-30/r4.anchor: وظاهر البدء في قوله { بدأكم } أول خلقة الإنسان الدنيوية لا مجموع الحياة الدنيوية قبال الحياة الأخروية

TABATABAI:7:29-30/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29-30/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:29-30/r5.claim: He rejects as the verse's primary sense the view that resurrection simply returns each person in the state in which he died, believer in faith and disbeliever in disbelief, because 'beginning' here concerns humanity's first creation.
TABATABAI:7:29-30/r5.anchor: كما يؤول إليه قول من قال

TABATABAI:7:29-30/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29-30/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:29-30/r6.claim: In context, God began humanity by decreeing two groups: people guided on the straight path and people who follow Iblis and go astray; they return divided as they were first begun.
TABATABAI:7:29-30/r6.anchor: فالمراد به كيفية البدء التي قصها في أول كلامه

TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r1.claim: The decree divides humanity between those beyond Iblis's power and those who follow him: 15:42 says Satan has no authority over God's servants except errant followers, while 22:4 says his allies are led astray.
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r1.anchor: هذا صراط علي مستقيم إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان إلا من اتبعك من الغاوين

TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r2.claim: The same split appears in 38:84: God swears to fill Hell with Iblis and those who follow him, then orders their descent and offers guidance in 20:123-124; following or rejecting it leads to safety or misery.
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r2.anchor: قال فالحق والحق أقول لأملأن جهنم منك وممن تبعك منهم أجمعين

TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r3.claim: Their misguidance follows their taking Satan as ally, rather than their alliance following an independently imposed misguidance; the decree is conditional on their allegiance.
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r3.anchor: وإنما قضي ضلالهم إثر اتباعهم وتوليهم لا بالعكس كما هو ظاهر الآية

TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r4.claim: The return-in-two-groups statement can explain the prior commands: act justly and sincerely so as to belong to God's guided party rather than those astray under Satan's guardianship.
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r4.anchor: فأقسطوا في أعمالكم وأخلصوا لله سبحانه حتى تكونوا من الفريق الذي هدى دون الفريق الذي حق عليهم الضلالة

TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r5.claim: A parallel is 2:148: although each person has an appointed direction, the command is still to race toward good; fixed destiny does not cancel the call to attain the happy destination through righteous action.
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r5.anchor: ولكل وجهة هو موليها فاستبقوا الخيرات أينما تكونوا يأت بكم الله جميعا

TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, 'as He began you, you return' may stand independently, while the surrounding context still alludes to a call to justice and sincere worship.
TABATABAI:7:29-30#2/r6.anchor: ومن الممكن أن يكون قوله { كما بدأكم } الخ

TABRISI:7:29-30/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:29-30/r1.claim: Qist is justice when directed toward truth and injustice when directed toward falsehood.
TABRISI:7:29-30/r1.anchor: أصل القسط العدل فإذا كان إلى جهة الحق فهو عدل ومنه قوله إن الله يحب المقسطين

TABRISI:7:29-30/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:29-30/r2.claim: Ikhlas is removing foreign admixture; sincerity to God means directing worship exclusively to Him.
TABRISI:7:29-30/r2.anchor: وأصل الإخلاص إخراج كل شائب من الجنس ومنه إخلاص الدين لله وهو توجيه العبادة إليه خالصا

TABRISI:7:29-30/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:29-30/r3.claim: Beginning is doing something for the first time and return is doing it a second time; a verb can also name an act's first phase.
TABRISI:7:29-30/r3.anchor: والبداء فعل الشيء أول مرة والعود فعله ثاني مرة وقد يكون فعل أول خصلة منه بدء

TABRISI:7:29-30/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:7:29-30/r7.claim: He coordinates “establish your faces” with the preceding prohibition against Satan, with an implied “beware Satan.”
TABRISI:7:29-30/r7.anchor: وأقيموا عطف على ما تقدم من قوله لا يفتننكم الشيطان فتقديره احذروا الشيطان وأقيموا وجوهكم عن أبي مسلم

TABRISI:7:29-30/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:29-30/r8.claim: An alternative parsing supplies “and say” after “my Lord commanded justice”: “My Lord commanded justice, and say: establish your faces.”
TABRISI:7:29-30/r8.anchor: وقيل: إن تقديره أمر ربي بالقسط وقل أقيموا

TABRISI:7:29-30/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:29-30/r9.claim: After clarifying that God does not command indecency, the passage identifies what He commands: qist, a comprehensive name for all good things.
TABRISI:7:29-30/r9.anchor: لما بين سبحانه أنه لا يأمر بالفحشاء وهو اسم جامع للقبائح والسيئات عقبه ببيان ما يأمر به من القسط

TABRISI:7:29-30/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30/r10.speaker: مجاهد والسدي وأكثر المفسرين
TABRISI:7:29-30/r10.claim: They explain qist as justice and uprightness.
TABRISI:7:29-30/r10.anchor: أي بالعدل والاستقامة عن مجاهد والسدي وأكثر المفسرين

TABRISI:7:29-30/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:7:29-30/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses qist as the declaration “there is no god but God.”
TABRISI:7:29-30/r12.anchor: وقيل: بلا إله إلا الله عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:7:29-30/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30/r13.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:7:29-30/r13.claim: Abu Muslim interprets qist as all acts of obedience and devotion.
TABRISI:7:29-30/r13.anchor: وقيل: بجميع الطاعات والقرب عن أبي مسلم

TABRISI:7:29-30/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30/r14.speaker: مجاهد والسدي وابن زيد
TABRISI:7:29-30/r14.claim: One reading is to face the qibla correctly at every mosque during prayer.
TABRISI:7:29-30/r14.anchor: أن معناه توجهوا إلى قبلة كل مسجد في الصلاة على استقامة عن مجاهد والسدي وابن زيد

TABRISI:7:29-30/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30/r15.speaker: الجبائي وغيره
TABRISI:7:29-30/r15.claim: Another reading directs worshippers toward the Kaaba, the direction God commanded; “mosque” means the times of prostration, or prayer times.
TABRISI:7:29-30/r15.anchor: أقيموا وجوهكم إلى الجهة التي أمركم الله بالتوجه إليها في صلاتكم وهي الكعبة والمراد بالمسجد أوقات السجود

TABRISI:7:29-30/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30/r16.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:7:29-30/r16.claim: If someone reaches a mosque at prayer time, they should pray there instead of waiting to return to their own mosque; here “mosque” is the place of prostration. Al-Maghribi prefers this view.

TABRISI:7:29-30/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:29-30/r17.claim: A fourth interpretation commands attending the mosque for each prayer and praying in congregation; most scholars consider this recommended, while a minority consider it obligatory.
TABRISI:7:29-30/r17.anchor: قصدوا المسجد في وقت كل صلاة أمر بالجماعة لهذا ندبا عند الأكثرين وحتما عند الأقلين

TABRISI:7:29-30/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30/r18.speaker: الربيع
TABRISI:7:29-30/r18.claim: Al-Rabi interprets the command as devoting oneself to God in obedience without associating an idol or anything else with Him.
TABRISI:7:29-30/r18.anchor: أخلصوا وجوهكم لله تعالى في الطاعة فلا تشركوا به وثنا ولا غيره عن الربيع

TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r1.claim: The command is to supplicate humbly to God after making religion sincere to Him.
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r1.anchor: وهذا أمر بالدعاء والتضرع إليه سبحانه على وجه الإخلاص أي أرغبوا إليه في الدعاء بعد إخلاصكم له الدين

TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r2.claim: An alternative interpretation takes “invoke Him” to mean worship Him with religion made sincere to Him.
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: معناه واعبدوه مخلصين له الدين

TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r3.claim: One connection is that sincere prayer matters because people will be resurrected and recompensed; the first creation should convince them of the second, even if resurrection seems implausible.
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r3.anchor: وادعوه مخلصين فإنكم مبعوثون ومجازون وإن بعد ذلك في عقولكم فاعتبروا بالابتداء

TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj connects the phrase with the preceding promise that people live, die, and emerge from the earth: resurrection is no harder than their initial creation, an argument against those denying resurrection.
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r4.anchor: أنه يتصل بقوله فيها تحيون وفيها تموتون ومنها تخرجون فقال كما بدأكم تعودون أي فليس بعثكم بأشد

TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r5.claim: Abu Muslim reads this as a new statement that God will recreate people after death and requite them.
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r5.anchor: أنه كلام مستأنف أي يعيدكم بعد الموت فيجازيكم عن أبي مسلم

TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r6.claim: Qatada says people began from earth and return to it, citing “From it We created you and into it We return you.”
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r6.anchor: قال قتادة: بدأكم من التراب وإليه تعودون كما قال منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم

TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r7.claim: Another interpretation compares resurrection with the first creation when people possessed nothing: they will likewise possess nothing when raised.
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: معناه كما بدأكم لا تملكون شيئا كذلك تبعثون يوم القيامة

TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وجابر
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and Jabir say people are raised in the state in which they died: believers in faith and disbelievers in disbelief.
TABRISI:7:29-30#2/r8.anchor: المؤمن على إيمانه والكافر على كفره عن ابن عباس وجابر

THALABI:v4p227/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p227/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p227/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets القسط as saying there is no god but God.
THALABI:v4p227/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بلا إله إلا الله

THALABI:v4p227/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p227/r10.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
THALABI:v4p227/r10.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi interpret القسط as justice.

THALABI:v4p227/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p227/r11.speaker: مجاهد والسدي وابن زيد
THALABI:v4p227/r11.claim: Mujahid, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd take this as facing the Kaaba in prayer wherever one is.
THALABI:v4p227/r11.anchor: قال مجاهد والسدي وابن زيد: يعني وجهوا وجوهكم حيث ما كنتم في الصلاة إلى الكعبة

THALABI:v4p227/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p227/r12.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v4p227/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak says that if prayer time arrives while one is at a mosque, pray there rather than preferring one’s own mosque; if no mosque is nearby, go to any mosque.
THALABI:v4p227/r12.anchor: وقال الضحاك: إذا حضرت الصلاة وأنتم عند المسجد فصلوا فيه ولا تقولن: أحب أن أصلي في مسجدي

THALABI:v4p227/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p227/r13.speaker: الربيع
THALABI:v4p227/r13.claim: Al-Rabiʿ interprets the command as directing worship and prostration sincerely to God alone, without idols or rivals.
THALABI:v4p227/r13.anchor: وقال الربيع: معناه واجعلوا سجودكم لله سبحانه وتعالى خالصا دون ما سواه من الآلهة والأنداد

THALABI:v4p227/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p227/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p227/r14.claim: Calling upon God means worshipping Him sincerely; religion here means obedience and worship.
THALABI:v4p227/r14.anchor: وادعوه واعبدوه مخلصين له الدين الطاعة والعبادة

THALABI:v4p227/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p227/r15.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v4p227/r15.claim: The Prophet says every soul will be resurrected in the state in which it had been.
THALABI:v4p227/r15.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «تبعث كل نفس على ما كانت عليه»

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses al-qist as the declaration that there is no god but God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (بلا إله إلا الله)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r4.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r4.claim: Al-Suddi also glosses al-qist as justice.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj says this command refutes the people's preceding claim that God had commanded their indecent practices.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج: (هذا رد لقولهم: {والله أمرنا بها} في الآية الأولى)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r6.speaker: أبو علي الجرجاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r6.claim: Abu Ali al-Jurjani says the imperative is coordinated with a declarative because the command of the Lord is itself speech: say that God commands justice and that you establish yourselves.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r6.anchor: قال أبو علي الجرجاني: (نسق الأمر على الخبر (¬6)، وجاز ذلك لأن قوله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r7.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r7.claim: Mujahid says to face the Kaaba in prayer wherever one is.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r7.anchor: وجهوا # وجوهكم (¬1) حيث ما كنتم في الصلاة إلى الكعبة، قال (¬2) مجاهد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r8.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r8.claim: Al-Suddi also interprets this as facing the Kaaba in prayer wherever one is.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r8.anchor: وجهوا # وجوهكم (¬1) حيث ما كنتم في الصلاة إلى الكعبة، قال (¬2) مجاهد (¬3) والسدي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd also interprets this as facing the Kaaba in prayer wherever one is.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r9.anchor: وجهوا # وجوهكم (¬1) حيث ما كنتم في الصلاة إلى الكعبة، قال (¬2) مجاهد (¬3) والسدي وابن زيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r10.claim: Ata reports from Ibn Abbas that the command means to pray to God alone in every mosque.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r10.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: (صلوا لله وحده في كل مسجد)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r11.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r11.claim: Al-Dahhak explains this to mean praying at any mosque where prayer time arrives, without insisting on one's own mosque.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r11.anchor: ما قاله الضحاك، وهو أنه قال: (إذا حضرت الصلاة وأنتم عند مسجد فصلوا فيه، ولا يقولن أحدكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r12.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r12.claim: Al-Farra gives the same instruction to pray at the mosque one is near when prayer time arrives.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r12.anchor: ونحو هذا قال الفراء؛ يقول (¬7): (إذا أدركتك الصلاة وأنت عند مسجد فصل فيه،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r13.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r13.claim: Abu Ishaq says to direct oneself to prayer at the time of every prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r13.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (أي (¬1): وقت كل صلاة اقصدوه بصلاتكم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r14.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r14.claim: To call upon God sincerely in religion means affirming His oneness and associating nothing with Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p89/r14.anchor: يريد: وحدوه ولا تشركوا به شيئا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God began Adam's children as believers and unbelievers and will resurrect each as such, citing 64:2.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (إن الله تعالى بدأ خلق ابن آدم مؤمنا و (¬4) كافرا،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r2.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r2.claim: Ata says those created for Paradise return to Paradise at resurrection, and those created for Hell return to Hell.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r2.anchor: قال عطاء: (يريد: من خلقه للجنة يعود في البعث إلى الجنة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r3.speaker: القرظي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r3.claim: Al-Qurazi says a person returns to the destiny on which God began him, even if his deeds seem to belong to the opposite destiny; he cites Iblis and sorcerers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r3.anchor: وقال القرظي (¬2): (من ابتدأ الله خلقه على (¬3) الشقوة، صار إلى ما ابتدأ عليه خلقه،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r4.claim: Al-Farra says people were initially created wretched or blessed and will return in that same state; the author says these destiny-based readings share one meaning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r4.anchor: قال الفراء: (يقول بدأكم (¬7) في الخلق شقيا وسعيدا، فكذلك تعودون على الشقاء والسعادة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r5.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r5.claim: Al-Hasan understands the verse to mean that people, first created from nothing in this world, will be brought back to life at resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد: (كما بدأكم فخلقكم في الدنيا, ولم تكونوا شيئا، كذلك تعودون يوم القيامة أحياء)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r6.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r6.claim: Mujahid shares the explanation that people, first created from nothing in this world, will be brought back to life at resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد: (كما بدأكم فخلقكم في الدنيا, ولم تكونوا شيئا، كذلك تعودون يوم القيامة أحياء)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r7.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers the creation-and-resurrection reading: the initial creation proves that resurrection is no more difficult, answering deniers of the resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r7.anchor: وهذا المعنى اختيار الزجاج؛ لأنه قال: (ثم احتج عليهم بإنكارهم البعث

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r8.claim: Ibn al-Anbari parses the kāf as an accusative object of تعودون, with the object advanced before its verb, meaning you return as your creation began.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r8.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: (موضع الكاف في {كما} نصب ب {تعودون} وهو على مذهب العرب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r9.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r9.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi says the phrase omits the noun creation: its sense is that creation is recreated as it was first begun, as in 21:104.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p91/r9.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي: (قوله: {كما بدأكم تعودون}، ليس معنى الكلام على الظاهر

QASHANI:7:29-30/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:29-30/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:29-30/r2.claim: Establishing one's face means keeping the self from excess or deficiency in justice and from spiritual fluctuation in uprightness.
QASHANI:7:29-30/r2.anchor: ذواتكم الموجودة بمنعها عن الميل والزيغ إلى طرفي الإفراط والتفريط في العدالة

QASHANI:7:29-30/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:29-30/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:29-30/r3.claim: A mosque here is each station of prostration or each time of prostration.
QASHANI:7:29-30/r3.anchor: أي: كل مقام سجود أو وقت سجود

QASHANI:7:29-30/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:29-30/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:29-30/r4.claim: The first prostration is submission and obedience: worship sincerely, avoid ostentation and hypocrisy, obey commands with truthful intent, and do not disobey.
QASHANI:7:29-30/r4.anchor: سجود الانقياد والطاعة وإقامة الوجه فيه بالإخلاص، والاجتناب عن الرياء والنفاق في العمل لله

QASHANI:7:29-30/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:29-30/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:29-30/r5.claim: The second prostration is annihilation in actions: fulfill its due while seeing neither oneself nor anything besides God as an agent.
QASHANI:7:29-30/r5.anchor: وسجود الفناء في الأفعال وإقامة الوجه فيه بالقيام بحقه بحيث لا يرى هو مؤثرا غير الله

QASHANI:7:29-30/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:29-30/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:29-30/r6.claim: The third prostration is annihilation in attributes, observing its conditions without self-admiration, while avoiding neglect of right action and anger at opponents.
QASHANI:7:29-30/r6.anchor: وسجود الفناء في الصفات، وإقامة الوجه عنده بالمحافظة على شرائطه

QASHANI:7:29-30/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:29-30/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:29-30/r7.claim: The fourth prostration is annihilation in essence: efface the remainder and ego-duality without falling into egoic excess or abandoning obedience.
QASHANI:7:29-30/r7.anchor: وسجود الفناء في الذات، وإقامة الوجه عنده بالغيبة عن البقية، والانطماس بالكلية

QASHANI:7:29-30/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:29-30/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:29-30/r8.claim: Sincerity at the first station dedicates action to God; at the second and third it sees religion and obedience as from God; at the fourth it sees through God.
QASHANI:7:29-30/r8.anchor: في المقام الأول بتخصيص العمل لله به، وفي الثاني والثالث برؤية الدين والطاعة من الله

QASHANI:7:29-30/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:29-30/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:29-30/r9.claim: At the final station, God is the one practicing religion, with no share in it for anyone else.
QASHANI:7:29-30/r9.anchor: فيكون الله هو المتدين بدينه ليس لغيره فيه نصيب

QASHANI:7:29-30/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:29-30/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:29-30/r10.claim: God began by making people manifest while hidden; they return by annihilation in Him and concealment so that He appears.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:28-31/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:28-31/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:28-31/r2.claim: God's command of justice refutes their claim that He commanded naked circumambulation; al-qist means justice.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:28-31/r2.anchor: رد لقولهم: { والله أمرنا بها } والقسط: العدل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:28-31/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:28-31/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:28-31/r3.claim: Orient yourselves toward the Kaaba wherever you are when praying.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:28-31/r3.anchor: وجهوا وجوهكم حيث ما كنتم في الصلاة إلى الكعبة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:28-31/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:28-31/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:28-31/r4.claim: Worship God alone and associate nothing with Him.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:28-31/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:28-31/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:28-31/r5.claim: As at creation, people are divided into the wretched and the blessed, and return as wretched or blessed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:28-31/r5.anchor: في الخلق شيقيا وسعيدا، فكذلك، { تعودون } سعداء وأشقياء

ELMALILI:7:26-30/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:26-30/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:26-30/r12.claim: God commands justice, worship with faces rightly oriented at every mosque and sincere religion devoted to Him, and promises that people will return as He first created them.
ELMALILI:7:26-30/r12.anchor: Rabbim adl ü insâfı emretti. Hem her mescidde yüzlerinizi doğru tutun ve O’na, dini mahza O’nun için hâlis kılarak ibadet edin. Sizi ibtidâ O yarattığı gibi yine O’na döneceksiniz

ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r14.claim: Qist means moderation and balance: avoid both excess and deficiency.
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r14.anchor: Rabbim kıst u itidâli emretti, yani ifrat u tefritten sakınıp itidal ve muvâzene ile hareket ediniz

ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r15.claim: Masjid is understood as each occasion or place of prostration, meaning prayer time or prayer place; worshippers face God and His qibla.
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r15.anchor: her secde zaman veya mekânında, her namaz veya namazgâhta yüzlerinizi dosdoğru O’na, O’nun kıblesine dikerek ibadetine teveccüh ediniz.

ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r16.claim: Pray wherever the prayer time arrives.
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r16.anchor: Namaz vakti nerede erişirse orada kılınız.

ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r17.claim: The congregation should turn uniformly to God under one rite, with no trace of shirk in their hearts or divergence in their faces.
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r17.anchor: kalblerinizde eser-i şirk, yüzlerinizde eser-i ihtilâf u i‘vicâc bulunmayarak muntazamen kılınız

ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r18.claim: Call on God and worship with sincere devotion to Him alone.
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r18.anchor: Allah için dininizde muhlis olarak, Allah’a dua ediniz

ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r19.claim: God will restore people to the afterlife just as He first created them, and returning them is easier than originating them.
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r19.anchor: Allah teâlâ siz insanları ibtidâ halk u inşâ edip dünyaya getirdiği gibi yine öyle iade edecek, âhirete gideceksiniz. Şüphe yok ki iade, ibtidâdan esheldir.

ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r20.claim: Those who deny the hereafter through naturalism should consider that what happened once can happen again, and that the God who originated creation is even more able to restore it.
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r20.anchor: tabiat kanunlarının başı bulunan “olan yine olur” kanununu düşünmeli ve ibdâya kādir olan Allah’ın iadeye evleviyetle kādir olduğunu anlayarak me‘âda inanmalıdırlar.

ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r21.claim: People came naked, will shed worldly clothing and return naked, and will receive recompense for their deeds.
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r21.anchor: dünya libâsından soyunup yine geldikleri gibi çırçıplak olarak dönüp gidecekler

ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r22.claim: God alone has power over origination and return; even rulers claiming to give life and death cannot create a child or take the life of an attacker.
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r22.anchor: أَنَا۠ أُحْىِۦ وَأُمِيتُ [el-Bakara 2/258] diyen nice nemrutlar gelmiş geçmiştir

ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r23.claim: Since God alone rules over beginning and return, people steadily approaching the hereafter should pray to Him alone with complete sincerity.
ELMALILI:7:26-30#2/r23.anchor: mebde’ ve me‘âdda hâkim münhasıran Allah olduğu için

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r1.claim: The previous verse censures people who attribute false beliefs, practices, and customs to God; following such traditions and claiming God commanded them are both wrong.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r1.anchor: Bir önceki âyette kendi yanlış inanç ve uygulamaları, bâtıl gelenekleri hakkında “Allah bize bunu emretti” diyenler ve böylece “Allah hakkında bilgisizce konuşanlar”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r2.claim: God commands the Prophet, and through him all people, to act justly; justice requires truth, balance, and moderation in belief and conduct.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r2.anchor: Oysa Allah peygamberine ve onun şahsında bütün insanlığa “adaleti emretmiştir.” Adalet, inançta ve yaşayışta doğruluğu, dengeli ve ölçülü olmayı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r3.speaker: İbn Abbas
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets qisṭ, justice, in this verse as accepting and affirming that there is no god but Allah.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r3.anchor: İbn Abbas bu âyetteki kıst (adalet) kelimesini “lâ ilâhe illallah”, yani “Allah’tan başka tanrı bulunmadığını kabul ve ikrar etmek”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r4.claim: Linking to 31:13, the commentary says associating partners with God is the greatest injustice; justice therefore means believing, saying, and practicing what is true.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r4.anchor: Bir âyette de (Lokmân 31/13) “O’na ortak koşmak kesinlikle çok büyük bir haksızlıktır” buyurulmuştur. Şu halde Allah adaleti

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r5.claim: People must not deify their ancestors, sanctify inherited wrongs as religion, serve the misguided regardless of their status, or frequent places of sin and rebellion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r5.anchor: insanlar atalarını putlaştırmasın; onlardan kalma çirkinlikleri, yanlış fikirleri, bozuk gelenekleri din gibi kutsallaştırmasın; görünüşteki değerleri, varlık ve mevkileri ne olursa olsun

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r6.claim: At every prostration, people are to turn toward God and call upon Him with sincere belief and devotion; as He first created them, they will return to Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r6.anchor: Her secde ettiğinizde yüzlerinizi O’na çevirin, kendisine içten bir inanç ve bağlılıkla O’na yalvarın! Başlangıçta sizi O yarattığı gibi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r7.claim: The closing warning says everyone’s final account will reveal whether they followed the indecent path of Meccan polytheists or the path of justice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:29/r7.anchor: insanların tuttuğu yolun, Mekkeli putperestlerinki gibi “fahişe” mi, yoksa “adalet” yolu mu olduğu hususunun sonunda mutlaka ortaya çıkacağı ve herkesin hesabının ona göre yapılacağı

QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r3.claim: Qist means justice, which applies in relation to God, other people, and oneself.
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r3.anchor: القسط العدل ، ويقع ذلك في حق الله تعالى ، وفي حق الخلق ، وفي حق نفسك

QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r4.claim: Justice toward God means keeping within the command without falling short in duties or committing prohibitions, withholding nothing entrusted to one, and preferring nothing over God among permitted things.
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r4.anchor: فالعدل في حق الله الوقوف على حد الأمر من غير تقصير في المأمور به أو إقدام على المنهي عنه

QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r5.claim: Justice toward other people means giving them fairness according to knowledge and, according to chivalry, relinquishing one’s own claim.
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r5.anchor: وأما العدل مع الخلق - فعلى لسان العلم - بذل الإنصاف ، وعلى موجب الفتوة ترك الانتصاف

QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r6.claim: Justice toward oneself means disciplining and restraining the soul, closing every door of ease to it, and opposing it in every circumstance and breath.
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r6.anchor: وأما العدل في حق نفسك فإدخال العتق عليها ، وسد أبواب الراحة بكل وجه عليها

QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r7.claim: Establishing one’s face and invoking God sincerely means sustaining awareness of His presence at every moment and in everything one does, leaves, advances, or delays.
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r7.anchor: الإشارة منه إلى استدامة شهوده في كل حالة ، وألا تنساه لحظة في كل ما تأتيه وتذره

QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r8.claim: Whomever God apportions happiness has a happy original disposition, state, and outcome; one whose allotment is the opposite has the reverse.
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r8.anchor: من كانت قسمته - سبحانه - له بالسعادة كانت فطرته على السعادة ، وكانت حالته بنعت السعادة

QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r9.speaker: رسول الله
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r9.claim: The Messenger says that a person will meet God in the condition in which that person was.
QUSHAYRI:v1p330/r9.anchor: قال رسول الله : ( من كان بحالة لقي الله بها )

BURHAN:v1p65/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p65/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p65/r4.claim: Although بدأ is the more eloquent triliteral form, يبدئ is apt beside يعيده because the matching quadriliteral forms create correspondence.
BURHAN:v1p65/r4.anchor: ونظيره فى مراعاة المناسبة أن الأفصح أن يقال بدأ ثلاثى قال الله تعالى

BURHAN:v2p25/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p25/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p25/r2.claim: One proof of bodily resurrection analogizes return to the initial creation: the one who began creation can repeat it.
BURHAN:v2p25/r2.anchor: أحدها قياس الإعادة على الابتداء قال تعالى

BURHAN:v3p263/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p263/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p263/r1.claim: Qur’anic paired terms commonly follow their derivational or temporal order, as with advance and delay, first and last, beginning and return, and before and after.
BURHAN:v3p263/r1.anchor: مراعاة اشتقاق اللفظ كقوله ﴿ لمن شاء منكم

BURHAN:v3p334/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p334/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p334/r8.claim: The final category shown shifts from past tense to command, as in قل أمر ربي بالقسط followed by وأقيموا, and the command after أحلت لكم الأنعام.

SULAMI:v1p226#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r1.claim: Junayd reads the command as guarding the secret, raising one's aspiration, and being content with God in place of everything else.
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r1.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه في هذه الآية : أمر بحفظ السر وعلو الهمة

SULAMI:v1p226#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r2.claim: Abu Uthman defines qist as truthfulness.

SULAMI:v1p226#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r3.speaker: رويم
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r3.claim: Ruwaym says sincerity in supplication means ceasing to see one's own actions.
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r3.anchor: قال رويم : إخلاص الدعاء أن ترفع رؤيتك عن أفعالك

SULAMI:v1p226#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r4.claim: Ibn Ata defines sincere supplication as that which is free of afflictions and defects.
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : إخلاص الدعاء ما خلص من الآفات

SULAMI:v1p226#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r5.speaker: حارث المحاسبي
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r5.claim: Al-Harith al-Muhasibi says sincerity removes creatures from one's dealings with God.
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r5.anchor: قال حارث المحاسبي : إخلاص الدعاء إخراج الخلق من معاملة الله

SULAMI:v1p226#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r6.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r6.claim: Abu Uthman says sincerity is forgetting creatures while continually looking toward the Creator.
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r6.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : الإخلاص نسيان رؤية الخلق لدوام النظر إلى الخالق

SULAMI:v1p226#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r7.claim: Another definition makes sincerity constant watchfulness and forgetting every self-serving interest.
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r7.anchor: قال بعضهم : الإخلاص دوام المراقبة ونسيان الحظوظ كلها

SULAMI:v1p226#2/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r8.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r8.claim: One explanation says Iblis began in disbelief but performed obedient acts before being returned to opposition, while the sorcerers began rightly, acted wrongly, and returned to their original state.
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r8.anchor: أبدأ خلقة إبليس على الكفر والخلاف ثم استعمله بأعمال المطيعين

SULAMI:v1p226#2/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r9.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r9.claim: Al-Husayn says God's decree concerning deeds does not change, since actions may accord with or oppose a person's original nature.
SULAMI:v1p226#2/r9.anchor: قال الحسين : في قوله : ﴿ كما بدأكم تعودون ﴾ لا تغيير لما أجرى عليه من الأعمال

ITQAN:v4p357/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p357/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p357/r2.claim: A scholar lists four proofs for bodily resurrection: analogy with first creation, the greater creation of the heavens and earth, revival of dead land, and fire produced from green trees.
ITQAN:v4p357/r2.anchor: وقال غيره استدل سبحانه وتعالى على المعاد الجسماني بضروب

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r1.speaker: النبي
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r1.claim: The Prophet’s saying warns against green growth on dung, an example of comparison whose intended likeness is intellectual.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r1.anchor: قول النبي إياكم وخضراء الدمن الشبه مأخوذ للمرأة من النبات

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r2.claim: The comparison does not concern a woman’s resemblance to a plant in color, taste, smell, shape, or bodily nature; it likens beauty from a bad upbringing to a plant on dung, attractive outside but corrupt within.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r2.anchor: بل القصد شبه عقلي بين المرأة الحسناء في المنبت السوء وبين تلك النابتة على الدمنة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r3.claim: The honey comparison is intellectual rather than sensory: agreement brings joy like sweetness, while opposition brings aversion and distress like bitterness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r3.anchor: فالتشبيه عقلي إذ ليس الغرض الحلاوة والمرارة اللتين تصفهما لك المذاقة ويحسهما الفم واللسان

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r4.claim: Calling a man the sun transfers the sun’s name to intellectual qualities such as eminence, rank, honor, and fame.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r4.anchor: ومن هذا الأصل استعارة الشمس للرجل تصفه بالنباهة والرفعة والشرف والشهرة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r5.claim: The expression نجوم الهدى calls the Prophet’s Companions stars because people find religious guidance through their knowledge, conduct, and example as travelers find routes by stars.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p51/r5.anchor: نجوم الهدى تعنى أصحاب رسول الله ورضى الله عنهم فانه استعارة توجب شبها عقليا

TUSTARI:7:29/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:29/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:29/r1.claim: Seek inward sincerity of intention in private, since only the sincere recognize ostentation.
TUSTARI:7:29/r1.anchor: اطلبوا من السر بالنية الإخلاص فإن الرياء لا يعرفه إلا المخلصون

TUSTARI:7:29/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:29/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:29/r2.claim: Make outward action follow the Prophet; whoever does not follow him in every affair is astray, and other approaches are misleading.
TUSTARI:7:29/r2.anchor: فإن من لم يكن اقتداؤه في جميع أموره بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فهو ضال،

DAMGHANI:v1p392/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p392/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p392/r1.claim: Aqīmū here means turn or orient your faces toward the qibla at every mosque.
DAMGHANI:v1p392/r1.anchor: أقيموا استقبلوا قوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p167/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p167/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p167/r1.claim: When prayer time comes and a person is at any mosque, he should pray there rather than wait to reach his own mosque.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p167/r1.anchor: {وأقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد} يقول: إذا حضرت الصلاة وأنتم عند مسجد من المساجد فصلوا فيه ولا يقولن أحدكم: لا أصلي حتى آتى مسجدي (1) .

MAJAZ:v1p213/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p213/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p213/r3.claim: Both occurrences of farīqan are accusative because the verb governs them; the second is conjoined to the first in case by proximity although it does not share its sense. Qur’an 76:31 gives a parallel.
MAJAZ:v1p213/r3.anchor: «كما بدأكم تعودون فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة» (28، 29) نصبهما جميعا على إعمال الفعل

MAJAZ:v1p213/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p213/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p213/r4.claim: The verb ḥaqqa is masculine although ḍalālah is feminine; Arabs use masculine verbs when separated from the feminine noun, as in “a night of the month passed.”
MAJAZ:v1p213/r4.anchor: وخرج فعل الضلالة مذكرا والعرب تفعل ذلك إذا فرقوا بين الفعل وبين المؤنثة لقولهم: مضى من الشهر ليلة

NAHHAS:v2p121/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p121/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p121/r10.claim: The kāf is accusative as comparison: people return as God first created them; Abu Ishaq attaches it to the preceding phrase about emerging from the earth.
NAHHAS:v2p121/r10.anchor: الكاف في موضع نصب أي تعودون كما بدأكم أي كما خلقكم

SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r1.claim: The strongest parse coordinates أقيموا with an understood imperative expanded from بالقسط: قل بأن أقسطوا وأقيموا.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r1.anchor: أنه معطوف على الأمر المقدر أي: الذي ينحل إليه المصدر

SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r2.claim: A verbal noun can unpack as أن plus past, present, or imperative when the verb is inflectable; the cited line اللبس عباءة وتقر عيني illustrates the present form.

SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r3.claim: Unlike أن, ما does not join to an imperative, and كي takes only the present; thus neither can unpack the مصدر with this command.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r3.anchor: وهذا بخلاف " ما " فإنها لا توصل بالأمر، وبخلاف " كي " فإنها لا توصل إلا بالمضارع

SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses وأقيموا وجوهكم as a command to aim yourselves toward worship.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r4.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " وأقيموا وجوهكم: وقل أقيموا وجوهكم أي: اقصدوا عبادته "

SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r5.claim: One analysis of al-Zamakhshari's gloss supplies a separate unspoken قل, with أقيموا governed by that command.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r5.anchor: فيكون " أقيموا " معمولا لقول أمر مقدر

SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r6.claim: Alternatively, أقيموا coordinates with أمر ربي, which is governed by قل; making قل explicit clarifies this attachment.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r6.anchor: فإنه معمول ل " قل ". وإنما أظهر الزمخشري

SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r7.claim: The author also allows coordination with an omitted command, estimated as قل أقبلوا وأقيموا.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r7.anchor: معطوفا على أمر محذوف تقديره: قل أقبلوا وأقيموا

SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r8.speaker: الجرجاني
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r8.claim: Al-Jurjani coordinates the command with the genitive بالقسط through meaning: قل أمر ربي means قل يقول ربي, as if God says اقسطوا وأقيموا.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r8.anchor: وقال الجرجاني صاحب " النظم ": " نسق الأمر على الجر، وجاز ذلك لأن قوله { قل أمر ربي } قول

SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says مسجد may mean at the time of each prostration or at the place of each prostration.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r9.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " في وقت كل سجود وفي مكان كل سجود "

SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r10.claim: The kasra pattern مسجد is irregular: the expected form has fatḥa on the middle radical, though it has many morphological parallels.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29/r10.anchor: وكان من حق مسجد مسجد بفتح العين

SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r1.claim: مخلصين is a circumstantial accusative for the subject of ادعوه; الدين is the object of the active participle, and له either attaches to مخلصين or modifies الدين as a circumstantial phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r1.anchor: و " له " متعلق بمخلصين، ويجوز أن يتعلق بمحذوف على أنه حال من " الدين "

SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r2.claim: Mekki gives two estimates for the omitted verbal noun; عودا مثل ما بدأكم fits the wording better than خروجا مثل ما بدأكم.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r2.anchor: ذكرهما مكي، والأول أليق بلفظ الآية الكريمة

SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r3.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r3.claim: The alternative estimate makes the phrase an adjective of an omitted مصدر, خروجا مثل ما بدأكم.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: تقديره يخرجون خروجا مثل ما بدأكم ذكرهما مكي

SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbari puts كما in the accusative with تعودون, treating it as a fronted object.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: " موضع الكاف في " كما " نصب بتعودون

SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r5.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r5.claim: Al-Farisi rejects a literal comparison of people to beginning: God restores creation as He first created it, with خلق omitted in both clauses.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r5.anchor: قال الفارسي " كما بدأكم تعودون " ليس على ظاهره إذ ظاهره

SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r6.claim: بدأ means initiated or originated and is used both as a triliteral verb and as أبدأ; 29:19 and 29:20 show both forms.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r6.anchor: ويستعمل بهذا المعنى ثلاثيا ورباعيا على أفعل

SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r7.claim: With باء, بدأ به means to put something first; ابتداء به has the same sense, and al-Raghib's أبدأت به is a rare form.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r7.anchor: وأما ما يتعدى بالباء نحو: بدأت بكذا بمعنى قدمته وجعلته أول الأشياء

SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r8.speaker: الراغب
