SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r8.claim: Al-Raghib additionally records the unusual form أبدأت به with the sense of putting something first.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r8.anchor: وحكى الراغب أيضا أنه يقال من هذا: أبدأت به على أفعل وهو غريب

SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r9.claim: أبدأت من أرض means I began departing from that land.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r9.anchor: وقولهم " أبدأت من أرض كذا " أي ابتدأت منها بالخروج

SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r10.claim: البدء can mean a chief; one explanation says he is counted first when notables are enumerated.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#2/r10.anchor: قيل: لأنه يبدأ به في العد إذا عد السادات

SAMIN-DURR:7:29#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#3/r1.claim: An anonymous line uses بدء for a leader who became chief only after his people died.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#3/r1.anchor: فجئت قبورهم بدءا ولما فناديت القبور فلم يجبنه

SAMIN-DURR:7:29#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#3/r2.claim: A second anonymous line parallels that sense: the speaker became master though no one had previously made him master.
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#3/r2.anchor: خلت الديار فسدت غير مسود ومن العناء تفردي بالسؤدد

SAMIN-DURR:7:29#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:29#3/r3.claim: ما in كما بدأكم is a مصدرية particle, yielding the sense like your first creation.

ZAJJAJ:v2p330/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p330/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p330/r3.claim: القسط means justice; what is just is recognized as sound by discerning people, so God's command of justice contradicts the claim that He commands grossly ugly deeds.
ZAJJAJ:v2p330/r3.anchor: أي بالعدل، فكيف يأمر بالفحشاء من يعلم أنه لا يفعل إلا الحكمة.

ZAJJAJ:v2p330#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p330#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p330#2/r1.claim: At every prayer time, direct yourselves to God through prayer.
ZAJJAJ:v2p330#2/r1.anchor: أي وقت كل صلاة اقصدوه بصلاتكم.

ZAJJAJ:v2p330#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p330#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p330#2/r2.claim: Being sincere in religion means being sincere in obedience to God.

ZAJJAJ:v2p330#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p330#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p330#2/r3.claim: The resurrection argument connects to the earlier statement that people live, die, and are brought forth from the earth: raising them is no harder than beginning their creation.
ZAJJAJ:v2p330#2/r3.anchor: وهو متصل بقوله: (فيها تحيون وفيها تموتون ومنها تخرجون). فقال: (كما بدأكم تعودون).

ASAD-NOTES:7:29#n21/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:29#n21/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:29#n21/r1.claim: Wajh, literally “face,” can figuratively mean a person's entire being or attention; Asad cites the phrase in 3:20 as an example.
ASAD-NOTES:7:29#n21/r1.anchor: The term wajh (lit., "face") occurring here is often used, in the abstract sense, to denote a person's entire being or entire attention

ASAD-NOTES:7:29#n21/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:29#n21/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:29#n21/r2.claim: Although masjid usually means the time or place of prostration, here and in 7:31 it signifies any act of worship.
ASAD-NOTES:7:29#n21/r2.anchor: evidently stands in this context - as well as in verse 31 below - for any act of worship

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p14/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p14/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p14/r2.claim: He reads masculine حق عليهم الضلالة as punishment: the return to the afterlife means people are not truly astray there, since everything is disclosed.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p14/r2.anchor: ونرى أنه في كل مرة يذكر فيها الضلالة بالتذكير تكون الضلالة بمعنى العذاب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p465/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p465/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p465/r2.claim: When الضلالة takes masculine agreement, the author reads it as punishment in the afterlife, where actual misguidance is absent because realities become clear.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p465/r2.anchor: في كل مرة يذكر فيها الضلالة بالتذكير تكون الضلالة بمعنى العذاب لأن الكلام في الآخرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p835/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p835/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p835/r3.claim: Masculine agreement with الضلالة signals punishment in the afterlife; feminine agreement signals worldly misguidance, since realities are disclosed in the hereafter.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p835/r3.anchor: في كل مرة يذكر فيها (الضلالة) بالتذكير تكون (الضلالة) بمعنى العذاب لأن الكلام في الآخرة

NASHR:v1p15#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p15#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p15#2/r1.claim: Calling every reading outside the seven readers or the famous manuals such as al-Shāṭibiyya and al-Taysīr anomalous is an ignorant misuse of the term.
NASHR:v1p15#2/r1.anchor: إطلاق من لا يعلم على ما لم يكن عن السبعة القراء، أو ما لم يكن في هذه الكتب المشهورة كالشاطبية والتيسير أنه شاذ

NASHR:v1p15#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p15#2/r8.speaker: بعض المتأخرين من شراح الشاطبية
NASHR:v1p15#2/r8.claim: Some later commentators’ Hamza-stop forms—pure yāʾ, wāw, or alif substitutions and deletions called رسمِي easing—are not valid reading variants.
NASHR:v1p15#2/r8.anchor: وقف حمزة على نحو (أسمايهم) و (أوليك) بياء خالصة، ونحو (شركاوهم) و (أحباوه)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p225#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p225#5/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p225#5/r1.claim: Qatāda explains that God first created people from nothing, then they died, and He will bring them back.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p225#5/r1.anchor: عن قتادة ﴿ كما بدأكم تعودون ﴾ قال كما بدأهم فخلقهم ولم يكونوا شيئا ثم ذهبوا ثم نعيدهم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p225#5/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p225#5/r2.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p225#5/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī says people return as God created them, believer or unbeliever, and are raised in the state in which they began.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p225#5/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي كما خلقهم كذلك يعودون من خلقه مؤمنا وكافرا أعاده كما بدأه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p225#5/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p225#5/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p225#5/r3.claim: Mujāhid specifies that the believer is raised a believer and the unbeliever an unbeliever.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p225#5/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قال يبعث المؤمن مؤمنا والكافر كافرا

ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r1.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r1.claim: Many define qist as justice or the balanced middle between excess and deficiency.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r1.anchor: والقسط على ما قاله غير واحد العدل وهو الوسط من كل شيء

ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r2.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r2.claim: Al-Rāghib defines qist as a just allotment; qasata means to take another’s share and be unjust, while aqsata means to give the share and act fairly.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r2.anchor: وقال الراغب هو النصيب بالعدل كالنصف والنصفة ويقال : القسط لأخذ قسط غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r3.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī says the root means inclination, fair when toward truth and unjust when toward falsehood; al-Ālūsī prefers al-Rāghib’s account.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r3.anchor: وهذا أولى مما قاله الطبرسي من أن أصله الميل

ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r4.claim: Abū Muslim takes the commanded justice to mean all acts of obedience and devotion.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r4.anchor: والمراد به هنا على ما نقل عن أبي مسلم جميع الطاعات والقرب

ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk interpret qist here as monotheism and the testimony “there is no god but God.”
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r5.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس والضحاك أنه التوحيد وقول لا إله إلا الله

ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r6.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r6.claim: Mujāhid, al-Suddī, and most exegetes take qist as uprightness and justice in affairs.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r6.anchor: ومجاهد والسدي وأكثر المفسرين على أنه الاستقامة والعدل في الأمور

ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r7.claim: Establishing one’s face means turning to worship of God uprightly, without turning toward other worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r7.anchor: أي توجهوا إلى عبادته تعالى مستقيمين غير عادلين إلى غيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r8.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r8.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī takes “at every mosque” as the time of each prostration; others take it as the place of prostration.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r8.anchor: في وقت كل سجود كما قال الجبائي أو مكانه كما قال غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r9.claim: On these readings, ʿinda means “in”; masjid is a time or place noun in its lexical sense, though its vowel pattern is exceptional, and sajda can stand metaphorically for prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r9.anchor: فعند بعنى في والمسجد اسم زمان أو مكان بالمعنى اللغوي

ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r10.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r10.claim: Many understand the command as obligatory: face the direction God prescribed for prayer, namely the Kaaba.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r10.anchor: وقال غير واحد : المعنى توجهوا إلى الجهة التي أمركم الله تعالى بالتوجه إليها

ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r11.speaker: المغربي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r11.claim: Al-Maghribī prefers praying at whichever mosque one reaches rather than delaying until returning to one’s own; he takes the command as recommended, though al-Ālūsī finds this remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r11.anchor: واختار المغربي أن المعنى إذا أدركتم الصلاة في أي مسجد فصلوا ولا تؤخروها

ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r12.claim: A related view makes this an exhortation to attend a mosque at every prayer; congregational prayer is recommended for some authorities and obligatory for others.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r12.anchor: ومثله ما قيل : إن المعنى اقصد المسجد في وقت كل صلاة على أنه أمر بالجماعة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r13.claim: Several syntactic analyses attach “establish” to an implied command within the preceding verbal noun, to the preceding statement as an imperative report, or to an omitted “say” or “turn.”
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r13.anchor: والواو للعطف وما بعده قيل معطوف على الأمر الذي ينحل إليه المصدر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r14.claim: “Call upon Him” may mean worship Him, since worship includes supplication, with dīn meaning obedience; alternatively it commands sincere supplication after sincere devotion.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p106#3/r14.anchor: فالدعاء بمعنى العبادة لتضمنها له والدين بالمعنى اللغوي وقيل

ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r1.claim: “As He began you, you return” means you return to God for recompense, so obey His commands or sincerely worship Him; it connects to the preceding command.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r1.anchor: إليه سبحانه فيجازيكم على أعمالكم فامتثلوا أوامره أو فأخلصوا له العبادة فهو متصل بالأمر قبله

ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r2.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj connects the phrase instead to 7:25, “in it you live,” though al-Ālūsī considers that connection remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج انه متصل بقوله تعالى ( فيها تحيون وفيها تموتون ومنها تخرجون ) ولا يخفى بعده

ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r3.claim: “You return” rather than “He restores you” hints that resurrection cannot be mistaken for happening without an agent; comparing it to the beginning establishes its possibility and God’s power.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r3.anchor: ولم يقل سبحانه يعيدكم كما الملائم لما قبله إشارة إلى أن الإعادة دون البدء من غير مادة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r4.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r4.claim: Qatāda says people return to dust just as they were created from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة المعنى كما بدأكم من التراب تعودون اليه كما قال سبحانه ( منها خلقناكم وفيها نعيدكم )

ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r5.claim: Another interpretation says that just as people began owning nothing, they will be resurrected owning nothing.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r5.anchor: وقيل المعنى كما بدأكم لا تملكون شيئا كذلك تبعثون يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r6.claim: Muḥammad b. Kaʿb says a person created for misery ultimately reaches it despite deeds resembling the saved, while one created for happiness reaches it despite contrary deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r6.anchor: وعن محمد بن كعب أن المراد أن من ابتدأ الله تعالى خلقه على الشقوة صار إليها

ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r7.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r7.claim: Al-Tirmidhī reports from ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ that the Prophet showed two registers of the people of Paradise and Hell, fixed their outcomes, told companions to strive rightly or near it because final deeds determine fate, then declared one group for Paradise and one for the Fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r7.anchor: مارواه الترمذي عن عمرو بن العاص قال خرج علينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وفي يده كتابان

ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r8.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r8.claim: A similar interpretation from Ibn Jubayr is “as it was written for you, so you will be.”
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r8.anchor: وقريب من هذا ما روي عن ابن جبير من أن المعنى كما كتب عليكم تكونون

ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says people return at resurrection as they began, believers and unbelievers, linking the phrase to the verse that some are unbelievers and some believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p107/r9.anchor: وروي عن الحبر أن المعنى كما بدأكم مؤمنا وكافرا يعيدكم يوم القيامة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses al-qist as the confession that there is no god but God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r5.anchor: {قل أمر ربي بالقسط} قال ابن عباس: بلا إله إلا الله،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بلا إله إلا الله، وقال الضحاك: بالتوحيد.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r7.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi gloss al-qist as justice.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد والسدي: بالعدل. {وأقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r8.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi say to turn faces toward the Kaaba in prayer wherever you are.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r8.anchor: قال مجاهد والسدي: يعني وجهوا وجوهكم حيث ما كنتم في الصلاة إلى الكعبة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r9.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak says that when prayer time comes and you are by a mosque, pray there rather than claim you will pray in your own mosque.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r9.anchor: وقال الضحاك: إذا حضرت الصلاة وأنتم عند مسجد فصلوا فيه ولا يقولن أحدكم أصلي في مسجدي.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r10.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r10.claim: Another explanation is to make your prostration sincere for God alone.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: معناه اجعلوا سجودكم لله خالصا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r11.anchor: وقيل: معناه اجعلوا سجودكم لله خالصا، {وادعوه} واعبدوه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r12.claim: Here الدين means obedience and worship.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas says God first created people as believers and unbelievers and will resurrect them in those states, citing 64:2.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r13.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إن الله تعالى بدأ خلق بني آدم مؤمنا وكافرا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r14.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r14.claim: Mujahid says people will be resurrected in the state in which they died.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r14.anchor: قال مجاهد: يبعثون على ما ماتوا عليه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r15.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r15.claim: The Prophet says every servant is resurrected in the state in which he died, believer in faith and unbeliever in unbelief.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r15.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "يبعث كل عبد على ما مات عليه، المؤمن على إيمانه والكافر على كفره"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r16.speaker: أبو العالية
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r16.claim: Abu al-Aliya says people return to the deeds they practiced among themselves.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r16.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: عادوا على عمله فيهم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r17.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r17.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r17.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says they will become as was decreed for them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r17.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: كما كتب عليكم تكونون.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r18.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r18.speaker: محمد بن كعب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r18.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says those created for wretchedness reach it despite righteous deeds, as Iblis did; those created for felicity reach it despite past evil, as the sorcerers did.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p223#2/r18.anchor: قال محمد بن كعب: من ابتدأ الله خلقه على الشقاوة صار إليها وإن عمل أهل السعادة

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r1.claim: Qisṭ is justice, the middle course in every matter, apart from excess and deficiency.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r1.anchor: بالعدل وهو الوسط من كل أمر

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r2.claim: The command means direct yourselves uprightly to worship without turning elsewhere, or face the qibla.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r2.anchor: وتوجهوا إلى عبادته مستقيمين غير عادلين إلى غيرها

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r3.claim: “At every mosque” can mean each time or place of prostration, namely prayer, or any mosque where prayer finds you, without delaying until return to your own mosque.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r3.anchor: في كل وقت سجود أو مكانه وهو الصلاة

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r4.claim: Calling upon God here means worshipping Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r4.anchor: واعبدوه. { مخلصين له الدين } أي الطاعة

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r5.claim: Dīn means obedience, since all return to God.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r6.claim: As God originated creation, He will recreate people to requite their deeds; likening return to beginning establishes resurrection’s possibility and God’s power, so worship should be sincere.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r6.anchor: وإنما شبه الإعادة بالإبداء تقريرا لإمكانها والقدرة عليها

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r7.claim: Other views say people return to soil, in their first naked and barefoot state, or as believers and unbelievers as first created.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:29/r7.anchor: وقيل كما بدأكم من التراب تعودون إليه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r5.claim: Qist is God's command to perform good deeds through the obligations He has imposed, countering their claim with sound reason supported by decisive transmission.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r5.anchor: بالقسط } وهو الأمر المحسن إلي بالتكليف بمحاسن الأعمال التي تدعو إليها الهمم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r6.claim: Worshippers should orient themselves sincerely at every place, time, and circumstance suitable for prostration, without restricting prayer to a particular mosque or time.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r6.anchor: عند كل مسجد } أي مكان ووقت وحال يصلح السجود فيه , ولا يتقيدزن أحد بمكان ولا زمان

BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r7.claim: Call upon God in worship, devoting religion wholly to Him and associating nothing with Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r7.anchor: وادعوه } عند ذلك كله دعاء عبادة { مخلصين له الدين } أي لا تشركوا به شيءا

BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r8.claim: As God began creation, He will resurrect people; they return divided into guided people, whose hearts He made receptive to guidance, and those upon whom misguidance is fixed.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r8.anchor: أي في النشأة الأولى فأنتم تبتدئون نعيدكم بعد الموت فأنتم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r10.claim: The repeated resurrection reminder addresses deniers by making them familiar with it and weakening their resistance, leading to the reminder that they will be brought out of the earth.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p23/r10.anchor: ولما كرر سبحانه ذكر البعث كما تدعو إليه الحكمة في تقرير ما ينكره المخاطب تأنيسا له به وكسرا لشوكته

DURR-FULL:v3p437/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r1.claim: Qatāda says God never honors a servant for disobedience, approves or commands it; He approves obedience and forbids disobedience.
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال: والله ما أكرم الله عبدا قط على معصيته ولا رضيها له ولا أمر بها ولكن رضي لكم بطاعته

DURR-FULL:v3p437/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {قل أمر ربي بالقسط} قال: بالعدل

DURR-FULL:v3p437/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r3.claim: Mujāhid says to face the Kaaba wherever one prays, whether in a church or elsewhere.
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {قل أمر ربي بالقسط} قال: بالعدل {وأقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد} قال: إلى الكعبة حيث صليتم في كنيسة أو غيرها

DURR-FULL:v3p437/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says to devote religion to God as humanity was first created in Adam's time, upon Islam, calling on no other; then face the Sacred House.
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r4.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله {وادعوه مخلصين له الدين كما بدأكم تعودون} يقول: اخلصوا له الدين كما بدأكم في زمان آدم حيث فطرهم على الإسلام

DURR-FULL:v3p437/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God first created Adam's descendants as believers and unbelievers, as in 64:2, and resurrects them in those same states.
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {كما بدأكم تعودون} الآية قال: إن الله بدأ خلق بني آدم مؤمنا وكافرا كما قال {هو الذي خلقكم فمنكم كافر ومنكم مؤمن} التغابن الآية 2

DURR-FULL:v3p437/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r6.speaker: جابر
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r6.claim: Jābir says people will be resurrected as they were: the believer in faith and the hypocrite in hypocrisy.
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r6.anchor: عن جابر في الآية قال: يبعثون على ما كانوا عليه المؤمن على ايمانه والمنافق على نفاقه

DURR-FULL:v3p437/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r7.claim: Mujāhid links returning as one was begun to the division into a guided group and a group doomed to error in 7:30.
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {كما بدأكم تعودون} {فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة}

DURR-FULL:v3p437/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r8.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r8.claim: Muḥammad b. Kaʿb says God brings each person back to the guidance or error on which He began creating them: the sorcerers died Muslim, while Iblīs returned to his original disbelief despite acting like angels; see 2:34.
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r8.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب في قوله {كما بدأكم تعودون} قال: من ابتدأ الله خلقه على الهدى والسعاده صيره إلى ما ابتدأ عليه خلقه كما فعل بالسحرة

DURR-FULL:v3p437/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also glosses the phrase as returning just as God created people the first time.
DURR-FULL:v3p437/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {كما بدأكم تعودون} يقول: كما خلقناكم أول مرة كذلك تعودون

DURR-FULL:v3p438/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God brought people to life from nothing, then makes them die and revives them on Resurrection Day.
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {كما بدأكم تعودون} قال: كما بدأكم ولم تكونوا شيئا فأحياكم كذلك يميتكم ثم يحييكم يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v3p438/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r2.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r2.claim: Al-Rabīʿ b. Anas says people were created from earth and return to earth.
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r2.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس في قوله {كما بدأكم تعودون} قال: خلقهم من التراب وإلى التراب يعودون

DURR-FULL:v3p438/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r3.speaker: مجهول
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r3.claim: An unattributed wisdom says no one should boast when created from earth and returning to it, or act arrogantly when alive today and dead tomorrow; God lowers the arrogant and raises the oppressed, as in 20:55.
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r3.anchor: وقيل في الحكمة: ما فخر من خلق من التراب وإلى التراب يعود وما تكبر من هو اليوم حي وغدا يموت

DURR-FULL:v3p438/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r5.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr says people will become as they were decreed: some guided and others condemned to error.
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير {كما بدأكم تعودون} قال: كما كتب عليكم تكونون {فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة}

DURR-FULL:v3p438/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r6.speaker: عمر بن أبي معروف
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r6.claim: ʿUmar b. Abī Maʿrūf transmits from an unnamed trustworthy man the gloss that people return uncircumcised and exposed.
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r6.anchor: عن عمر بن أبي معروف قال: حدثني رجل ثقة في قوله {كما بدأكم تعودون} قال: قلفا بظرا

DURR-FULL:v3p438/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r7.speaker: مقاتل بن وهب العبدي
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r7.claim: Muqātil b. Wahb al-ʿAbdī says this verse will come to pass at the end of this community.
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r7.anchor: عن مقاتل بن وهب العبدي أن تأويل هذه الآية {كما بدأكم تعودون} تكون في آخر هذه الأمة

DURR-FULL:v3p438/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r8.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says God transforms many creatures when they sin privately in contempt of Him, then resurrects them as humans before admitting them to Hell; al-Suyūṭī cites al-Bukhārī's al-Ḍuʿafāʾ.
DURR-FULL:v3p438/r8.anchor: عن عبد الغفور بن عبد العزيز بن سعيد الأنصاري عن أبيه عن جده أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن الله تعالى يمسخ خلقا كثيرا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1462/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1462/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1462/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses “justice” as fairness; al-Suddī, Mujāhid, and Qatāda agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1462/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : بالقسط قال : بالعدل . وروى عن السدى : ومجاهد وقتادة مثل ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1462/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1462/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1462/r2.claim: Mujāhid says to turn toward the Kaʿba wherever one prays, even in a church or elsewhere.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1462/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد : قوله : واقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد : إلى الكعبة حيث صليتم ، في كنيسة أو غيرها

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1462/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1462/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1462/r3.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says God created people upon Islam in Adam's time, so they should invoke Him alone, devote religion, prayer, and deeds to Him, and face the Sacred House.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1462/r3.anchor: عن الربيع عن أبي العالية : وادعوه مخلصين له الدين

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1463/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1463/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1463/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that people return just as God created them the first time.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1463/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : كما بداكم تعودون يقول : كما خلقناكم اول مرة كذلك تعودون

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1463/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1463/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1463/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says people return as they were created, emerging from their mothers' wombs.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1463/r2.anchor: عن السدى : قوله : كما بداكم تعودون كما خلقناكم كذلك تعودون ، تخرجون من بطون امهاتكم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1463/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1463/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1463/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr interprets the phrase as meaning that people will be as was decreed for them.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1463/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال : كما كتب عليكم تكونون

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1463/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1463/r4.speaker: النخعي؛ ابن رزين
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1463/r4.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī and Ibn Razīn say people return to God's knowledge of them.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1463/r4.anchor: عن النخعي وابن رزين قالا : إلى علمه تصيرون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r1.claim: After denying that God commands indecency in 7:28, the verse digresses to state the foundations of true religion; repeating “say” without a conjunction stresses this important contradiction of their claim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r1.anchor: فصلت هذه الجملة عن التي قبلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r2.claim: Qist means justice broadly: the balanced virtue in an act, free of excess and deficiency, and sound for welfare in both the near and long term.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r2.anchor: أي الفعل الذي هو وسط بين الإفراط والتفريط في الأشياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r3.claim: Examples of justice as a mean include monotheism between association and denial, just retaliation between impunity and collective vengeance, and beneficence between miserliness and extravagance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r3.anchor: والقصاص من القاتل عدل بين إطلال الدماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses qist as the declaration “There is no god but God”; Ibn ʿĀshūr explains that this means monotheism is among the greatest forms of justice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن القسط قول لا إلاه إلا هو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r5.claim: Clothing and food likewise require moderation: dress should cover nakedness and protect from heat or cold, while food should avoid both excessive restriction and gluttonous indulgence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r5.anchor: والعدل هو اللباس الذي يستر العورة ويدفع أذى القر أو الحر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r6.claim: This comprehensive command to justice refutes every claim that God commanded their indecent practices, since none of those acts is just.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p86#3/r6.anchor: كلام جامع لإبطال كل ما يزعمون أن الله أمرهم به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r1.claim: The command coordinates with “My Lord commands justice” and tells the audience explicitly to do the opposite of certain alleged divine commands; commanding the opposite also implicitly forbids them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r1.anchor: أي قل لأولئك المخاطبين أقيموا وجوهكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r2.claim: “Establish your faces” pictures complete attention to worship, like someone facing an important sight without turning right or left.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r2.anchor: وإقامة الوجوه تمثيل لكمال الإقبال على عبادة الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r3.claim: To establish the face means to make it firmly and actively oriented; “standing” can denote strength in action, as in saying that a market or prayer stood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r3.anchor: وهو في إطلاق القيام على القوة في الفعل كما يقال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r4.claim: God commands reverent worship at sacred places, not nakedness or other invented forms of honoring Him; associating idols with God in worship contradicts this command.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r4.anchor: ولم يأمر بتعظيمه ولا تعظيم مساجده بما سوى ذلك مثل التعري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r5.claim: A hadith supports reverence in prayer: the worshipper converses with his Lord and should not spit in front of himself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r5.anchor: المصلي يناجي ربه فلا يبصقن قبل وجهه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r6.claim: Here “masjid” means any place set aside for worship; in Islamic usage it became the name of a specific, bounded place for prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r6.anchor: عند كل مكان متخذ لعبادة الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r7.claim: Since the audience then had no mosques apart from pilgrimage sanctuaries, the command concerns the Hajj rites and requires worshipping God alone there.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r7.anchor: ولم يكن لهم مساجد غير شعائر الحج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r8.claim: Polytheists placed Hubal on the Kaaba for the circumambulation, Isāf and Nāʾila at Ṣafā and Marwa for the saʿy, and some invoked Manāt at al-Mushallal; the command rejects these associations.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r9.claim: This command follows the denial that God commands indecency and the affirmation that He commands justice; it addresses polytheists, while believers must persist in it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p87#2/r9.anchor: عقب إنكار أن يأمر الله بالفحشاء من أحوالهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r1.claim: “Call upon Him” means worship Him, as in the verse about those whom people worship besides God.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r2.claim: Sincerity is purifying something from mixture; dīn here means obedience, from the expression “I obeyed so-and-so.” God is al-Dayyān, who subdues and makes all beings compliant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r2.anchor: والإخلاص تمحيض الشيء من مخالطة غيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r3.claim: “Sincere to Him in religion” is a circumstantial phrase attached to the pronoun in “worship Him.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r3.anchor: و { مخلصين } حال من الضمير في ادعوه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r4.claim: The parallel command in 98:5 confirms that the aim is to eliminate associating partners in worship, thereby realizing the justice named earlier in this verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r4.anchor: والمقصد منها إبطال الشرك في عبادة الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r5.claim: “As He began you, you will return” is an estimated circumstantial clause from the implied subject of “sincere”: worship with your return to God in view.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r5.anchor: مقدرين عودكم إليه وأن عودكم كبدئكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r6.claim: The warning focuses on returning to God to be judged for insincere worship and association; the comparison with the first creation recalls the resurrection they denied.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r6.anchor: وأدمج فيه قوله : { كما بدأكم } تذكيرا بإمكان البعث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r7.claim: The second creation is no more difficult than the first, as 50:15 and 30:27 argue against their supposed reason for rejecting resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r7.anchor: بأن ذلك الخلق ليس بأعجب من خلقهم الأول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r8.claim: God alone created them initially and will create them again, so He alone recompenses them and their idols can do nothing for them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p88#2/r8.anchor: فهو منفرد بالجزاء فلا يغني عنهم آلهتهم شيئا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p89#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p89#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p89#2/r1.claim: The kāf compares their return in creation to their beginning; mā is infinitival, yielding “you return with a new return like His beginning you.”

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p89#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p89#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p89#2/r2.claim: The comparison phrase precedes its verb, “you return,” to give the comparison prominence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p89#2/r2.anchor: على فعله ، وهو تعودون ، للاهتمام به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r1.claim: “My Lord commands justice” implies “act justly”; وأقيموا is coordinated with the implied command.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r1.anchor: تضمن قوله قل أمر ربي بالقسط أقسطوا ولذلك عطف عليه قوله وأقيموا حملا على المعنى،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r3.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi understand this as facing the Kaaba, establishing the qibla and requiring adherence to it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r3.anchor: فقيل أراد إلى الكعبة قاله مجاهد والسدي والمقصد على هذا شرع القبلة والأمر بالتزامها،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r4.speaker: الربيع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r4.claim: Al-Rabi says this means intending God in every prayer and directing oneself to Him; “face” means aim, not the organ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r4.anchor: وقيل أراد الأمر بإحضار النية لله في كل صلاة والقصد نحوه كما تقول وجهت وجهي لله قاله الربيع.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r5.claim: On al-Rabi's reading, face means aim and direction, not the physical organ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r5.anchor: فلا يؤخذ الوجه على أنه الجارحة بل هو المقصد والمنزع،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r6.claim: Another view permits prayer anywhere on earth, wherever people establish their orientation to God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: المراد بهذا اللفظ إباحة الصلاة في كل موضع من الأرض، أي حيث ما كنتم فهو مسجد لكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r7.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r7.claim: Some say the occasion was that people prayed only in their own mosques and qibla, refusing to pray at other mosques.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r7.anchor: قال قوم: سببها أن قوما كانوا لا يصلون إلا في مساجدهم في قبلتهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r8.claim: مخلصين is circumstantial to the subject of وادعوه; الدين is its object.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r8.anchor: وقوله مخلصين حال من الضمير في وادعوه، والدين مفعول ب مخلصين.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r9.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r9.claim: Hasan, Qatada, Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid take this as resurrection: God recreates people after death; pause after تعودون.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r9.anchor: قال الحسن بن أبي الحسن وقتادة وابن عباس ومجاهد: المراد بقوله: كما بدأكم تعودون الإعلام بالبعث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو العالية ومحمد بن كعب ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير والسدي وجابر بن عبد الله والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r10.claim: Another view, also reported in meaning from the Prophet, says worldly groups decreed wretched or blessed remain so in the afterlife; God's decrees do not change, so no pause after تعودون.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وأبو العالية ومحمد بن كعب ومجاهد أيضا وسعيد بن جبير والسدي وجابر بن عبد الله وروي معناه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r11.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r11.claim: Ubayy ibn Kab's reading explicitly says people return as two groups, one guided and one astray.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p391#2/r11.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي بن كعب «تعودون فريقين فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak say that when prayer time arrives near a mosque, one should pray there rather than insist on one's own mosque.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r1.anchor: أحدها إذا حضرت الصلاة وأنتم عند مسجد فصلوا فيه ولا يقولن أحدكم أصلي في مسجدي قاله ابن عباس والضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba prefers this instruction to pray at whichever mosque is nearby when prayer time comes.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r3.speaker: مجاهد والسدي وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r3.claim: Mujahid, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd understand the command as facing the Kaaba in prayer wherever one is.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r3.anchor: والثاني توجهوا حيث كنتم في الصلاة إلى الكعبة قاله مجاهد والسدي وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r4.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r4.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas says to make prostration sincere for God alone.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r4.anchor: والثالث اجعلوا سجودكم خالصا لله تعالى دون غيره قاله الربيع بن أنس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r5.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r5.claim: Al-Mawardi reads the verse as a command to attend the mosque at every prayer time and pray in congregation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r5.anchor: والرابع اقصدوا المسجد في وقت كل صلاة أمرا بالجماعة لها ذكره الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r6.claim: One explanation of calling upon God is worship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r6.anchor: قولان أحدهما أنه العبادة والثاني الدعاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r7.claim: The other explanation of calling upon God is supplication.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r7.anchor: قولان أحدهما أنه العبادة والثاني الدعاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r8.claim: One explanation is to devote worship solely to God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r8.anchor: قولان أحدهما مفردين له العبادة والثاني موحدين غير مشركين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r9.claim: Another explanation is to affirm God's unity without associating partners with Him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r9.anchor: قولان أحدهما مفردين له العبادة والثاني موحدين غير مشركين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r10.claim: One view says people will be resurrected in the states in which they began, fortunate or wretched; it is transmitted from Ibn Abbas and held by early authorities.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r10.anchor: أحدها كما بدأكم سعداء وأشقياء كذلك تبعثون روى هذا المعنى علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r11.claim: Another view says God restores people as His power first created them; al-Zajjaj links this to living and dying in the earth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r11.anchor: والثاني كما خلقتم بقدرته كذلك يعيدكم روى هذا المعنى العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r12.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r12.claim: Al-Mawardi says that just as people began with nothing of their own, they return without possessing anything.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p185/r12.anchor: والثالث كما بدأكم لا تملكون شيئا كذلك تعودون ذكره الماوردي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r1.anchor: وقوله: {قل أمر ربي بالقسط} أي: بالعدل والاستقامة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r2.claim: The command is to worship uprightly in its proper places by following the messengers in what they conveyed of God's reports and laws, and to worship God sincerely; acceptance requires both conformity to the law and freedom from shirk.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r2.anchor: أي: أمركم بالاستقامة في عبادته في محالها، وهي متابعة المرسلين المؤيدين بالمعجزات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r3.claim: Mujāhid, through Ibn Abī Najīḥ, interprets the phrase as God bringing people to life after death.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r3.anchor: قال ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {كما بدأكم تعودون} يحييكم بعد موتكم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r4.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī says that just as people began in worldly life, they will return alive on the Day of Resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: كما بدأكم في الدنيا، كذلك تعودون يوم القيامة أحياء.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r5.claim: Qatāda explains that God first created people from nothing, then they died, and then He will recreate them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: {كما بدأكم تعودون} قال: بدأ فخلقهم ولم يكونوا شيئا، ثم ذهبوا، ثم يعيدهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r6.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r6.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam says God will bring people back at the end as He first began them; Ibn Jarīr chooses this view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r6.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: كما بدأكم أولا كذلك يعيدكم آخرا. واختار هذا القول أبو جعفر بن جرير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet said people will be gathered barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised, as God first created them; the report is in both Ṣaḥīḥs and also transmitted by al-Bukhārī via al-Thawrī.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قام فينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بموعظة فقال: "يا أيها الناس، إنكم تحشرون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r8.claim: Mujāhid, in a report from Waqāʾ ibn Iyās, says a Muslim is resurrected as a Muslim and a disbeliever as a disbeliever.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r8.anchor: وقال وقاء بن إياس أبو يزيد، عن مجاهد: {كما بدأكم تعودون} قال: يبعث المسلم مسلما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r9.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r9.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya interprets the return as people being returned to God's prior knowledge of them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r9.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: {كما بدأكم تعودون} ردوا إلى علمه فيهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r10.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr gives two wordings: people return as decreed for them, or as they had been and will be.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r10.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: {كما بدأكم تعودون} كما كتب عليكم تكونون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r11.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r11.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī says those created for wretchedness end there even if they act like the blessed, as Iblis did, while those created for bliss end there even if they act wickedly, as the sorcerers did.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p402#3/r11.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي في قوله تعالى: {كما بدأكم تعودون} من ابتدأ الله خلقه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r1.claim: Al-Suddī says people return just as created: one group guided and one astray, brought forth from their mothers' wombs in those conditions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r1.anchor: وقال السدي: {كما بدأكم تعودون. فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة} يقول: {كما بدأكم تعودون}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr reconciles predestination with the creation-fitra reports: all were created with knowledge and oneness of God, while belief and disbelief arise later, and God decrees both the blessed and wretched.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r6.anchor: ووجه الجمع على هذا أنه تعالى خلقهم ليكون منهم مؤمن وكافر، في ثاني الحال، وإن كان قد فطر الخلق كلهم على معرفته وتوحيده،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r7.claim: The Prophet says every child is born on the fitra, but the parents make the child Jewish, Christian, or Magian; al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmit it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "كل مولود يولد على الفطرة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r8.speaker: عياض بن حمار عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r8.claim: In a report in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, God says He created His servants upright, then Satan diverted them from their religion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r8.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم، عن عياض بن حمار (9) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "يقول الله تعالى:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r9.claim: Ibn Kathīr also cites the hadith that each person goes forth either freeing or destroying himself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p404/r9.anchor: وفي الحديث: "كل الناس يغدو، فبائع نفسه فمعتقها، أو موبقها"

JISHUMI:v4p2538/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r2.claim: Qist means justice, associated etymologically with turning toward the direction of truth and uprightness; turning toward falsehood is injustice.
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r2.anchor: القسط: العدل، وأصله من العدول، كأنه عدول إلى جهة الحق والاستقامة،

JISHUMI:v4p2538/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r3.claim: Abu Muslim says justice is a comprehensive name for everything praiseworthy.
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r3.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: العدل: اسم يجمع كل محمود.

JISHUMI:v4p2538/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r4.claim: The commentary cites God’s love of those who act justly and the statement that the unjust will be fuel for Hell as related uses of the root.
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r4.anchor: ومنه: (إن الله يحب المقسطين)، وإذا مال إلى الباطل فهو جور، ومنه: (وأما القاسطون فكانوا لجهنم حطبا)

JISHUMI:v4p2538/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r5.claim: Beginning is doing something for the first time; badaʾtu and abdaʾtu are two equivalent forms.
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r5.anchor: والبدء: فعل الشيء أول مرة، وبدأت بالأمر وأبدأت بمعنى، وهما لغتان،

JISHUMI:v4p2538/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r6.claim: Returning is doing something a second time; God is the initiator and restorer, and restoration applies to what remains of God’s act when it was not caused by something else.
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r6.anchor: والعود: فعل الشيء ثاني مرة، والله المبدئ المعيد، ومنه: عاد يعود، والإعادة إنما تجوز على ما يبقى من فعل الله إذا لم يكن عن سبب.

JISHUMI:v4p2538/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r12.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r12.claim: Abu Muslim connects ‘establish your faces’ syntactically to the preceding wording, with the sense ‘beware Satan and do not obey him.’
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r12.anchor: وأقيموا وجوهكم، عن أبي مسلم. وقيل: تقديره

JISHUMI:v4p2538/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r13.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r13.claim: One parsing supplies an omitted conjunction and verbal noun: ‘and [He commanded] that you establish.’
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r13.anchor: وقيل: تقديره: أمر ربي بالقسط، وبأن تقيموا.

JISHUMI:v4p2538/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r14.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r14.claim: Another parsing supplies a repeated ‘say’: ‘Say, my Lord commands justice, and say: establish your faces.’
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r14.anchor: وقيل: تقديره: قل أمر ربي بالقسط، وقل: أقيموا وجوهكم،

JISHUMI:v4p2538/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r16.speaker: أبو مسلم والقاضي
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r16.claim: The verse follows the denial that God commands indecency by naming the comprehensive good He commands, justice, then moving to promise and threat.
JISHUMI:v4p2538/r16.anchor: قيل: لما بين أنه لا يأمر بالفحشاء كما زعم الكفار، وهو اسم جامع للقبائح، عقبه ببيان ما يأمر به،

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r4.claim: Qist means either truth or justice.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r4.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : بالصدق . والثاني : بالعدل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r5.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r5.claim: Mujahid interprets the command as facing the Kaaba in prayer wherever one is.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r5.anchor: أحدها : معناه توجهوا حيث كنتم في الصلاة إلى الكعبة , قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r6.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r6.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas reads it as directing one's prostration sincerely to God, apart from idols and images.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r6.anchor: والثاني : معناه اجعلوا سجودكم خالصا لله تعالى دون ما سواه من الأوثان والأصنام , قاله الربيع بن أنس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r7.claim: A third interpretation commands attending the mosque at each prayer for congregation; most regard this as recommended, while a minority consider it obligatory.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r7.anchor: والثالث : معناه اقصدوا المسجد في وقت كل صلاة , أمرا بالجماعة لها , ندبا عند الأكثرين , وحتما عن الأقلين .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r8.claim: Another interpretation says to pray wherever prayer time finds you, since that place is a mosque, and not delay prayer until reaching a mosque.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r8.anchor: والرابع : أن أي موضع أدركت فيه وقت الصلاة فصل فيه فإنه مسجد ولا تؤخرها إلى حضور المسجد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r9.claim: Calling on God sincerely may mean affirming His oneness and sincere obedience, or seeking Him in supplication after making religion sincere for Him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r9.anchor: يحتمل وجهين : أحدهما : يعني أقروا له بالوحدانية وإخلاص الطاعة . والثاني : ارغبوا إليه في الدعاء بعد إخلاصكم له الدين .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says people will be resurrected in the same state of felicity or wretchedness in which they began.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r10.anchor: أحدها : كما بدأكم شقيا وسعيدا , كذلك تبعثون يوم القيامة , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r11.claim: Another account says people began as believers or unbelievers and will be resurrected accordingly; a Prophetic report says every soul is raised in its lived state.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r11.anchor: الثاني : كما بدأكم فآمن بعضكم وكفر بعضكم , كذلك تبعثون يوم القيامة . روى أبو سفيان عن جابر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( تبعث كل نفس على ما كانت عليه ) .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r12.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r12.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd say that just as God created people from nothing, He will revive them after they perish.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r12.anchor: الثالث : كما خلقكم ولم تكونوا شيئا , كذلك تعودون بعد الفناء أحياء , قاله الحسن , وابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r13.claim: A final view says people will return with no possessions; a report from Ibn Abbas says they are gathered barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised, with Abraham first clothed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p216/r13.anchor: الرابع : كما بدأكم لا تملكون شيئا , كذلك تبعثون يوم القيامة . روى سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( يحشر الناس يوم القيامة حفاة عراة غرلا

MUJAHID:v1p234#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p234#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p234#2/r1.claim: At every place of prayer, face toward the Kaaba, including when praying in a church or elsewhere.
MUJAHID:v1p234#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ وأقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد ﴾ يقول اجعلوا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد إلى الكعبة حيث ما صليتم في كنيسة أو غيرها

MUJAHID:v1p235/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p235/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p235/r1.claim: Mujahid explains the return as dividing into the felicitous and the wretched: one party guided and one party liable to error.
MUJAHID:v1p235/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ كما بدأكم تعودون ﴾ ﴿ فريقا هدى وفريقا حق عليهم الضلالة ﴾ يعني شقيا وسعيدا

MUQATIL:7:26-29/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:26-29/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:26-29/r11.claim: The Lord's command to act justly means to act with justice.

MUQATIL:7:26-29/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:26-29/r12.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:26-29/r12.claim: Establishing one's face means turning toward the qibla; at any mosque, church, synagogue, or other place of worship, pray facing the Kaaba.
MUQATIL:7:26-29/r12.anchor: يعنى وأمر ربى أن تقيموا وجوهكم، يعنى إلى القبلة، { عند كل مسجد } فى بيعة أو كنيسة أو غيرها، فصلوا قبل الكعبة

MUQATIL:7:26-29/r13.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:26-29/r13.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:26-29/r13.claim: Calling on God sincerely means affirming His oneness; He commanded prayer and monotheism.
MUQATIL:7:26-29/r13.anchor: وأمرهم بالصلاة والتوحيد، فذلك قوله: { وادعوه مخلصين } ، يعنى موحدين

MUQATIL:7:26-29/r14.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:26-29/r14.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:26-29/r14.claim: People return to God just as He created them happy or wretched.
MUQATIL:7:26-29/r14.anchor: يعنى كما خلقكم سعداء وأشقياء كذلك تعودون

NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r1.claim: Qisṭ means justice and what every rational person recognizes as good, so God cannot command indecency.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r1.anchor: بالعدل وبما هو حسن عند كل عاقل فكيف يأمر بالفحشاء

NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r2.claim: The command may mean to direct yourselves uprightly to God’s worship without turning elsewhere at every prayer time or place of prostration.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r2.anchor: ﴿ وأقيموا وجوهكم عند كل مسجد ﴾ وقل أقيموا وجوهكم أى اقصدوا عبادته

NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r3.claim: «Call upon Him» here means worship Him.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r4.claim: Sincerity means obedience done purely while seeking God’s face.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r4.anchor: أى الطاعة مبتغين بها وجهه خالصا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p9/r5.claim: As God first created people, He will resurrect them to recompense their deeds; initial creation refutes denial of resurrection.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses al-qist as the declaration that there is no god but Allah.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لا إله إلا الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r2.claim: Another view takes al-qist as justice: God commands justice, so obey Him; the wording contains an ellipsis.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r2.anchor: وقيل: القسط العدل أي أمر بالعدل فأطيعوه. ففي الكلام حذف.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r3.claim: Direct yourselves toward the qibla in every prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r3.anchor: أي توجهوا إليه في كل صلاة إلى القبلة.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r4.claim: The instruction applies wherever a mosque is located.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r4.anchor: { عند كل مسجد } أي في أي مسجد كنتم.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r5.claim: Call on God sincerely, affirm His oneness, and associate no partner with Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r5.anchor: { وادعوه مخلصين له الدين } أي وحدوه ولا تشركوا به.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r6.claim: The return echoes 6:94, where people come singly as first created.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r6.anchor: ولقد جئتمونا فرادى كما خلقناكم أول مرة

QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r7.claim: The comparative kaf is accusative: people return as God first created them.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r7.anchor: والكاف في موضع نصب أي تعودون كما بدأكم أي كما خلقكم أول مرة يعيدكم.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r8.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj attaches the phrase to what precedes: from it you emerge, and just as God began you, you return.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:29-30/r8.anchor: وقال الزجاج: هو متعلق بما قبله. أي ومنها تخرجون كما بدأكم تعودون.

BURSEVI:v3p115#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p115#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p115#2/r6.claim: Qist means justice and the balanced middle of a thing, beyond excess and deficiency.
BURSEVI:v3p115#2/r6.anchor: والقسط العدل وهو الوسط من كل شيء المتجاوز عن طرفي الإفراط والتفريط

BURSEVI:v3p115#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p115#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p115#2/r7.claim: A report says the best matters are in the middle; a Persian verse likewise says both extremes are blameworthy.

BURSEVI:v3p115#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p115#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p115#2/r8.claim: وأقيموا is coordinated with أمر with an implied قل, avoiding coordination of an imperative with an indicative.
BURSEVI:v3p115#2/r8.anchor: معطوف على أمر بتقدير قل لئلا يلزم عطف الإنشاء على الأخبار

BURSEVI:v3p115#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p115#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p115#2/r9.claim: The command means either turn steadfastly toward worship without turning elsewhere, or face the qibla.

BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r1.claim: عند كل مسجد may denote a time or place; sujūd stands for the whole prayer by naming a part for the whole.
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r1.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون اسم زمان ، وأن يكون اسم مكان أي في كل وقت سجود

BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r2.speaker: الكلبي
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says to pray at whichever mosque one reaches when prayer time comes, rather than insist on one's own; if none is nearby, go to any mosque.
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي : معناه إذا حضرت الصلاة وأنتم في مسجد فصلوا فيه

BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r3.claim: Al-Furūʿ says the neighborhood mosque is preferable to the congregational mosque if its imam is learned; market workers should pray by the shop by day and home at night.
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r3.anchor: وفي الفروع : مسجد المحلة أفضل من الجامع إذا كان الإمام عالما

BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r4.speaker: الحدادي
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r4.claim: Al-Haddadi reads the verse as requiring obligatory prayer in congregation; a hadith exempts those with an excuse who hear the call but do not answer.
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r4.anchor: قال الحدادي : وهذه الآية تدل على وجوب فعل الصلاة المكتوبة في الجماعة

BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r5.claim: Congregational prayer earns 27 degrees over solitary prayer, associated with 17 obligatory and 10 regular daily rak‘ahs.
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r5.anchor: وصلاة الجماعة أفضل من صلاة الفذ بسبع وعشرين درجة

BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r6.speaker: العلماء
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r6.claim: Scholars say mosque prayer is better than home congregation for rites such as obligatory prayer and tarawih because it displays Islam's symbols; home congregation exceeds praying alone at home.
BURSEVI:v3p115#3/r6.anchor: قال العلماء : كل ما شرعت فيه الجماعة كالفرائض والتراويح ونحوهما فالمسجد فيه أفضل

BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r1.claim: دعاء means worship here: a specific act names the broader category; supplication is a gateway to worship, whose core is humble dependence on God.
BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r1.anchor: أي : واعبدوه فهو من إطلاق الخاص على العام فإن الدعاء من أبواب العبادة

BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r2.claim: Dīn means obedience, since people return to God in the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r2.anchor: أي : الطاعة فإن مصيركم إليه في الآخرة

BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r3.claim: The Persian verse warns the traveler not to be deceived when reality becomes clear after performing only metaphorical or insincere acts.
BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r3.anchor: فردا كه يشكاه حقيقت شود بديد شر منده رهروى كه عمل بر مجاز كرد

BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r4.claim: God originated you and will recreate you for judgment; the comparison describes an omitted verbal noun, returning as He first created you.
BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r4.anchor: {كما بدأكم} أي : أنشأكم ابتداء {تعودون} إليه بإعادته

BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r5.claim: Resurrection is possible: whoever originated creation can repeat it, and raising people is no harder than creating them initially.
BURSEVI:v3p115#4/r5.anchor: وإنما شبه الإعادة بالإبداء تقريرا لإمكانها والقدرة عليها

RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r1.claim: The command to justice follows the account of God forbidding indecency and shows that God commands equity.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r1.anchor: لما بين أمر الأمر بالفحشاء بين تعالى أنه يأمر بالقسط والعدل

RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r2.claim: The phrasing suggests justice is good in itself because of qualities belonging to it, and God commands it on that basis; al-Razi refers to his prior answer on intrinsic goodness.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r2.anchor: وذلك يدل أيضا على أن الحسن إنما يحسن لوجوه عائدة إليه

RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r3.speaker: عطاء
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r3.claim: Ata and al-Suddi explain qist as justice and what reason plainly recognizes as good and correct.

RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says qist means the testimony that there is no deity but God, citing 3:18 as evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : هو قول لا إله إلا الله

RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r5.claim: Al-Razi identifies the first command as the shahada, encompassing knowledge of God's essence, acts, rulings, and oneness.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r5.anchor: وهو يشتمل على معرفة الله تعالى بذاته وأفعاله وأحكامه

RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r6.claim: To coordinate the command with the preceding statement, supply another 'say': 'Say: My Lord commands justice, and say: establish your faces...'.

RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r7.claim: Among readings of establishing one's face, al-Razi prefers facing the qibla, since sincerity is stated afterward.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r7.anchor: والأقرب هو الأول ، لأن الإخلاص مذكور من بعد

RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r8.claim: He rejects interpreting the phrase as sincerity because the next command already says to call on God sincerely, making that reading repetitious and incoherent.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48/r8.anchor: ولو حملناه على معنى الإخلاص ، صار كأنه قال : وأخلصوا عند كل مسجد

RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r1.claim: Although sincerity might attach only to supplication, the phrase can apply to both commands and should not be restricted, especially since religion covers all acts of devotion.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r1.anchor: لما أمكن رجوعه إليهما جميعا ، لم يجز قصره على أحدهما

RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r2.claim: The phrase could refer to prayer time or place; the place-based reading is an alternative to al-Razi's preferred time-based reading.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r2.anchor: اختلفوا في أن المراد منه زمان الصلاة أو مكانه

RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r3.claim: Al-Razi prefers prayer time: believers should face the Kaaba wherever they pray rather than privilege particular locations.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r3.anchor: والأقرب هو الأول ، لأنه الموضع الذي يمكن فيه إقامة الوجه للقبلة

RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says to pray at any mosque where one is when prayer time arrives, rather than insisting on one's clan's mosque.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : المراد إذا حضرت الصلاة وأنتم عند مسجد فصلوا فيه

RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r5.claim: Al-Razi says the verse requires facing at every mosque but does not establish a prohibition on leaving one mosque for another.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r5.anchor: لأن لفظ الآية يدل على وجوب إقامة الوجه في كل مسجد ، ولا يدل

RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r6.claim: Al-Razi takes calling on God sincerely as the acts of prayer: prayer literally means supplication, and its noblest parts are supplication and remembrance.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r6.anchor: والأظهر عندي أن المراد به أعمال الصلاة ، وسماها دعاء

RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r7.claim: The requirement to worship God sincerely parallels 98:5.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r7.anchor: ونطيره قوله تعالى : { وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا الله مخلصين له الدين }

RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says people return as God began them: believers are raised believers and unbelievers unbelievers, according to the happiness or misery for which they were created and acted.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { كما بدأكم } خلقكم مؤمنا أو كافرا

RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r9.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r9.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid say that just as God created people from nothing in this world, He will resurrect them alive.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r9.anchor: قال الحسن ومجاهد : { كما بدأكم } خلقكم في الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r10.claim: Supporters of Ibn Abbas cite the next verse's division into a guided party and a party bound for error as explaining this return.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r10.anchor: احتجوا على صحته بأنه تعالى ذكر عقيبه قوله : { فريقا هدى

RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r11.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r11.claim: Al-Qadi objects that nobody says God first made us believers or unbelievers, since faith and unbelief must arise later.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r11.anchor: قال القاضي : هذا القول باطل ، لأن أحدا لا يقول

RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r12.claim: Al-Razi calls the objection weak: 'beginning' can mean beginning in faith or unbelief, happiness or misery, and the same state holds at resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r12.anchor: وهذا السؤال ضعيف ، لأن جوابه أن

RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r13.claim: The passage orders the shahada, then prayer, and says their benefit appears in the afterlife, as in God's instructions to Moses in 20:14–15.
RAZI-FULL:v14p48#2/r13.anchor: ثم بين أن الفائدة في الإتيان بهذه الأعمال ، إنما تظهر في الدار الآخرة
